  201	impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {
  209	        for table in schema.tables.values_mut() {
  210	            let mut recorded = 0;
  211	            table.constraints.retain(|constraint| {
  212	                if let Constraint::Capabilities(names) = constraint {
  213	                    carriers += 1;
  214	                    declared.extend(names.iter().cloned());
  215	                    false
  216	                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
  217	                    recorded += 1;
  219	                } else { true }
  220	            });
  221	            if recorded > 1 || (recorded != 0 && table.recorded.is_empty()) {
  222	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));
  223	            }
  224	            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
  225	        }
  226	        for name in &declared {
  227	            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {
  228	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability {name}; upgrade the engine/device")));
  229	            }
  230	        }
  231	        let mut required = schema.required_capabilities();
  232	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
  233	        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
  234	        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
  235	        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
  236	        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
  237	            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");
  238	        // The price carrier can be absent in an old projection. Missing prices
  239	        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
  240	        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
  242	            else { required.remove(cap); }
  243	        }
  244	        // Stores written before the digest migration have no carrier for this
  245	        // capability. Admit that persisted schema for server-side rebuilding;
  246	        // its next serialization stamps the capability, so old devices refuse.
  247	        let mut legacy_semantic_capabilities = BTreeSet::new();
  248	        if !declared.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1")
  249	            && required.remove("maintained-id-sha256-v1") {
  250	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("maintained-id-sha256-v1".into());
  251	        }
  252	        // Kept pre-Wave-12 schemas need the server's new expiry action path,
  253	        // then stamp the device fence on their next published projection.
  254	        if !declared.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1")
  255	            && required.remove("expiry-reference-actions-v1") {
  256	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("expiry-reference-actions-v1".into());
  257	        }
  258	        // Before the shared fence, the binder emitted Recorded on F2 tables
  259	        // even when the same schema also declared timelines. Only that legacy
  260	        // representation infers its full requirements; modern carriers remain
  261	        // exact, including when mixed with a legacy marker.
  262	        if legacy && carriers == 0 {
  263	            // A legacy marker only covers the capabilities that predate the fence.
  264	            // New semantics must never inherit permission from this escape hatch.
  265	            declared = required.iter().filter(|name| matches!(name.as_str(),
  266	                "maintained-column" | "recorded-attribution" | "timeline" | "timeline-v2")).cloned().collect();
  267	        }
  268	        if declared != required || carriers + usize::from(legacy) != usize::from(!required.is_empty()) {
  269	            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: schema requires {required:?}, but declares {declared:?} in {carriers} carriers")));
  270	        }
  271	        let had_prices = !schema.source_reservations.is_empty();
  272	        schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
  273	        // Opening an old blob preserves its wire shape. Complete visible
  274	        // declarations can still price a write on demand; hidden ones cannot.
  275	        if !had_prices { schema.source_reservations.clear(); }
  276	        schema.legacy_receipt_prediction = legacy_receipt_prediction
  277	            || (!declared.contains("source-write-reservations-v1") && !schema.receipts.is_empty());
  278	        schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities = legacy_semantic_capabilities.into();
  279	        Ok(schema)
  280	    }

  328	                let mut admission=Meter::new(Ceilings::job(),Cut::Abort);admission.heap((r.get::<_,i64>(0)?.max(0) as u64).saturating_mul(64).saturating_add(8192))?;
  329	                let definition:Backfill=decode(&r.get::<_,String>(1)?)?;
  330	                if let Some(receipt)=evidence(tx,t,id,&definition.key())? {
  340	            for entering in next.downfills.iter().filter(|f|f.table==fill.table) {
  341	                if let Some(e)=evidence(tx,t,id,&entering.down_key())? {if !e.active {forward_outputs.extend(e.reversed.into_keys());}}
  342	            }
  343	            let mut pruned_outputs=BTreeSet::new();
  344	            let mut q=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT octet_length(d.definition),d.definition FROM _backfill_pruned p JOIN _backfill_definitions d ON d.digest=p.definition WHERE p.t=?1 AND p.id=?2 ORDER BY p.definition")?;
  345	            let mut receipts=q.query(params![t,id])?;
  346	            while let Some(r)=receipts.next()? {
  347	                let mut admission=Meter::new(Ceilings::job(),Cut::Abort);admission.heap((r.get::<_,i64>(0)?.max(0) as u64).saturating_mul(64).saturating_add(8192))?;
  348	                pruned_outputs.extend(decode::<Backfill>(&r.get::<_,String>(1)?)?.outputs);
  349	            }
  350	            drop(receipts);drop(q);
  351	            if target_outputs.iter().any(|c|pruned_outputs.contains(c)) {bad.add(id,"forward predecessor preimage was explicitly pruned");return Ok(())}
  352	            let mut projected_outputs=BTreeSet::new();
  353	            for c in &target_outputs {
  354	                if forward_outputs.contains(c){continue}
  355	                // An active receipt means this cell was supplied by this down
  356	                // declaration on the preceding rollback.  Its archived copy
  366	                // the explicit down declaration is the author's substitution
  367	                // policy for that otherwise ambiguous evidence-free case.
  368	                let retained=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_values WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND column_name=?3 AND data!=?4)",params![t,id,c,canonical_json(&Value::Null)],|r|r.get::<_,bool>(0))?;
  369	                // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — an identical-type rename presents the current business value in the old spelling.
  370	                if !retained || fill.name.starts_with("$rename:down:") {projected_outputs.insert(c.clone());}
  371	            }
  372	            if projected_outputs.len()<target_outputs.len(){preimages+=1;if preimage_ids.len()<5{preimage_ids.push(id.to_owned());}}
  373	            if projected_outputs.is_empty(){return Ok(())}
  374	            if prior.is_none() && tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _backfill_pruned WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND definition=?3)",params![t,id,key],|r|r.get::<_,bool>(0))? {
  375	                bad.add(id,"reverse projection evidence was explicitly pruned");return Ok(())
  376	            }
  377	            let native_source=row_source(tx,t,id,sources.get(&fill.table))?;
  378	            if let Some(source)=native_source.as_deref() {if let Some(c)=projected_outputs.iter().find(|c|source.columns.get(*c).is_some_and(protected)||source_owned(source,c)) {
  379	                bad.add(id,&format!("native preimage {}.{c} requires reference, asset or lifetime custody; keep a typed bridge",fill.table));return Ok(())
  380	            }}
  414	    }
  415	    Ok(true)
  416	}
  417	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#191-declared-old-views-and-renames — all down expressions observe the assembled newer snapshot before any forward preimage is restored.
  418	fn apply_staged_downfills(tx:&Tx<'_>)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
  419	    let mut stmt=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT t,id,definition,patch,evidence,octet_length(patch)+octet_length(evidence) FROM temp._downfill_pending ORDER BY t,id,definition")?;let mut rows=stmt.query([])?;
  420	    while let Some(r)=rows.next()? {let t:i64=r.get(0)?;let id:String=r.get(1)?;let key:String=r.get(2)?;

  435	    let _source_mask=SourceMask(tx);
  436	    for fill in &next.backfills {
  437	        fill.admit(next).map_err(refusal)?;

  439	                if fill.inputs.len()!=1 || fill.outputs.len()!=1 {return Err(refusal("generated column rename must have exactly one input and output"))}

  444	        }
  445	        if let Some(old)=sources.get(&fill.table) {for c in &fill.outputs {

  448	            }
  457	    }
  458	    // A name is immutable within a continuous lineage. Replacing a transform
  459	    // deliberately goes through an old-source/bridge transition first.

  462	    // Names keep one meaning throughout durable store history, including gaps

  468	        let old:Backfill=decode(&row.get::<_,String>(1)?)?;
  469	        if let Some(new)=next.backfills.iter().find(|f|f.table==old.table && f.name==old.name && f.key()!=old.key()) {
  470	            return Err(refusal(format!("backfill {} {} changed historical meaning; old digest {}; new digest {}; use a new name in a bridge release",old.table,old.name,old.key(),new.key())));
  471	        }
  472	    }
  473	    let mut known_down=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT octet_length(definition),definition FROM _downfill_definitions ORDER BY digest")?;

  477	        let old:Backfill=decode(&row.get::<_,String>(1)?)?;

  490	    let down_pending=if let Some(previous)=previous{stage_downfills(tx,next,previous,sources,now,report)?}else{false};

  770	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — pruning is a loss of migration evidence, not a way to reset immutable declaration names.
  771	pub(super) fn prune_warnings(tx:&Tx<'_>)->Result<Vec<String>,RuntimeError>{
  772	    if !present(tx)? {return Ok(Vec::new())}
  773	    let mut outputs:BTreeMap<String,BTreeSet<String>>=BTreeMap::new();
  774	    let mut q=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT d.definition FROM _backfill_definitions d WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _backfill_evidence e WHERE e.definition=d.digest)")?;
  775	    for definition in q.query_map([],|r|r.get::<_,String>(0))? {
  776	        let f:Backfill=decode(&definition?)?;
  777	        outputs.entry(f.table).or_default().extend(f.outputs);
  778	    }
  779	    let mut warnings=Vec::new();
  780	    let mut q=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT d.digest,d.definition,EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _backfill_evidence e WHERE e.definition=d.digest) FROM _downfill_definitions d ORDER BY d.digest")?;
  781	    for definition in q.query_map([],|r|Ok((r.get::<_,String>(0)?,r.get::<_,String>(1)?,r.get::<_,bool>(2)?)))? {
  782	        let (_,definition,has_receipt)=definition?;let f:Backfill=decode(&definition)?;
  783	        if has_receipt || outputs.get(&f.table).is_some_and(|fields|!fields.is_disjoint(&f.outputs)) {
  784	            warnings.push(format!("prune blinds down {} {}: its reverse/native or predecessor preimages will be discarded; future rollback or forward may refuse; retain history or restore a backup. Prune does not reset declaration names or digests",f.table,f.name));
  785	        }
  786	    }
  787	    Ok(warnings)
  788	}

  790	// Prune forgets historical values, retaining only the fact that exact reversal
  791	// is no longer available. No tombstone can be queried by an app.
  792	pub(super) fn prune(tx:&Tx<'_>)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
  793	    if present(tx)? {tx.conn().execute_batch("DELETE FROM _backfill_evidence WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE r.t=_backfill_evidence.t AND r.id=_backfill_evidence.id); DELETE FROM _backfill_pruned WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE r.t=_backfill_pruned.t AND r.id=_backfill_pruned.id); INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _backfill_pruned(t,id,definition,active,retained_outputs) SELECT t,id,definition,active,retained_outputs FROM _backfill_evidence; DELETE FROM _backfill_evidence; DELETE FROM _backfill_absence WHERE (definition!='' AND definition NOT LIKE '$native:%') OR NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE r.t=_backfill_absence.t AND r.id=_backfill_absence.id);")?;}
  794	    Ok(())
  795	}

 1076	fn physical_value(tx:&Tx<'_>,t:i64,id:&str,row:&Value,column:&str,meter:&mut Meter)->Result<Option<Value>,RuntimeError>{
 1077	    if let Ok(value)=row.field(column){meter.heap(value.retained_heap_bytes().saturating_mul(64).saturating_add(8192))?;return Ok(Some(value.clone()));}
 1078	    if tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name='_asset_column_renames')",[],|r|r.get::<_,bool>(0))? {
 1079	        let aliases:Vec<String>=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT name FROM _asset_column_renames WHERE t=?1 AND origin=(SELECT origin FROM _asset_column_renames WHERE t=?1 AND name=?2) ORDER BY name")?.query_map(params![t,column],|r|r.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
 1080	        for alias in aliases {if let Ok(value)=row.field(&alias){meter.heap(value.retained_heap_bytes().saturating_mul(64).saturating_add(8192))?;return Ok(Some(value.clone()));}}
 1081	    }

    7	/// Conservative input-domain inclusion: every value accepted by old is accepted by new.
    8	pub fn accepts(old: &A, new: &A) -> bool {
    9	    accepts_in(old,new,None,None)
   10	}

   12	fn accepts_in(old: &A, new: &A, old_bound: Option<&Bound>, new_bound: Option<&Bound>) -> bool {
   13	    if old==new {return true;}
   14	    match (old,new) {
   15	        (A::Optional(a),A::Optional(b))=>accepts_in(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
   16	        (A::Optional(_),_)=>false,
   17	        (a,A::Optional(b))=>accepts_in(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
   35	}

   38	enum ResultChange { Same, Additive, Changed }
   39	
   40	fn combine(fields: impl IntoIterator<Item=ResultChange>, extra: bool) -> ResultChange {
   41	    let mut additive=extra;
   42	    for field in fields {
   43	        match field {ResultChange::Changed=>return ResultChange::Changed,ResultChange::Additive=>additive=true,ResultChange::Same=>{}}
   44	    }
   45	    if additive {ResultChange::Additive} else {ResultChange::Same}
   46	}

   54	fn map_change<T>(old: &BTreeMap<String,T>, new: &BTreeMap<String,T>, compare: impl Fn(&T,&T)->ResultChange) -> ResultChange {
   55	    combine(old.iter().map(|(name,old)|new.get(name).map(|new|compare(old,new)).unwrap_or(ResultChange::Changed)),new.len()>old.len())
   56	}

   58	fn result_change(old: &Ty, new: &Ty, old_bound: &Bound, new_bound: &Bound) -> ResultChange {
   59	    if result(old,old_bound)==result(new,new_bound) {return ResultChange::Same;}
   60	    match (old,new) {
   61	        (Ty::Optional(a),Ty::Optional(b))|(Ty::Omittable(a),Ty::Omittable(b))
   62	        |(Ty::List(a,_),Ty::List(b,_))|(Ty::Collection(a,_),Ty::Collection(b,_))=>result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
   63	        (Ty::Object(a)|Ty::RowShape(a)|Ty::RowObject(a),Ty::Object(b)|Ty::RowShape(b)|Ty::RowObject(b))=>map_change(a,b,|a,b|result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound)),
   64	        (Ty::Row(a),Ty::Row(b)) | (Ty::WriteRow(a),Ty::WriteRow(b)) | (Ty::Page(a,_),Ty::Page(b,_)) if a==b=>{
   65	            let (Some(a),Some(b))=(table_fields(a,old_bound),table_fields(b,new_bound)) else{return ResultChange::Changed;};
   66	            combine(a.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if b.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),b.len()>a.len())
   67	        }
   68	        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
   69	    }
   70	}

   72	fn action_result_change(old: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>, new: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>) -> ResultChange {
   73	    match (old,new) {
   74	        (None,None)=>ResultChange::Same,
   75	        (Some(old),Some(new))=>combine(old.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if new.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),new.len()>old.len()),
   76	        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
   77	    }
   78	}

  116	pub fn compare(old: &Bound, new: &Bound, label: &str) -> Vec<String> {
  117	    let mut lines=Vec::new();
  118	    for before in old.programs.iter().filter(|p|p.program.kind!=ProgramKind::Job) {
  119	        let name=&before.program.name;

  121	        let Some(after)=new.programs.iter().find(|p|p.program.name==*name) else {
  122	            lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed operation; old calls get E_OP; keep `alias {name} = replacement` for a same-module query/mutation, or retain a wrapper"));continue;
  123	        };
  124	        if before.program.kind!=after.program.kind {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: operation kind changed; retain the old endpoint kind"));continue;}
  125	        let rename_candidate = |new_kind: &A| before.program.args.iter().find(|(old_name, old_kind)|
  126	            !after.program.args.contains_key(*old_name) && !after.program.arg_aliases.contains_key(*old_name)
  127	                && accepts_in(old_kind,new_kind,Some(old),Some(new)));

  130	            if before.program.args.contains_key(arg) { continue; }

  132	                if !accepts_in(old_kind,kind,Some(old),Some(new)) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: aliased argument {old_arg} → {arg} narrows the old input domain ({old_kind:?} → {kind:?}); retain the old input domain or a compatible wrapper"));}
  133	            } else if !matches!(kind,A::Optional(_)) {
  134	                if let Some((old,_))=rename_candidate(kind) {
  135	                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: required argument {old} appears renamed to {arg}; old calls get E_INPUT; declare `{arg}: <new type> alias {old}` if it is the same value, or retain a compatible wrapper"));
  136	                    warned_renames.insert(old.clone());
  137	                } else {
  138	                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: clients calling without new required argument {arg} get E_INPUT; give {arg} a fitting `default <literal>` or retain a compatible wrapper"));
  139	                }
  140	            }
  141	        }
  142	        for (arg,kind) in &before.program.args {
  143	            match after.program.args.get(arg) {

  147	                },

  151	                _=>{}
  152	            }
  153	        }
  154	        for (alias,canonical) in &before.program.arg_aliases {
  155	            let old_kind=&before.program.args[canonical];
  156	            let next=after.program.args.get(alias).or_else(||after.program.arg_aliases.get(alias).and_then(|name|after.program.args.get(name)));
  157	            match next {

  159	                Some(kind) if !accepts_in(old_kind,kind,Some(old),Some(new))=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: argument alias {alias} retyped or narrowed ({old_kind:?} → {kind:?}); retain its old input domain")),
  160	                _=>{}
  161	            }
  162	        }

  167	                if let Some(target)=target {

  169	                        lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: independent arguments {prior} and {canonical} now share {target}; old calls containing both positions get E_INPUT; retain separate arguments or a compatible wrapper"));
  170	                    }

  173	        }

  178	            for field in before_table.columns.keys().filter(|f|!before_table.read_optional(f)&&after_table.read_optional(f)) {
  179	                lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: {table}.{field} is now audience-optional; handle an omitted row property or a null explicit scalar before adopting the new column read rule"));

  185	        match change {

  187	            ResultChange::Changed=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: result shape/value domain changed; preserve the old projection/domain or introduce a new operation before retiring old clients")),
  188	            ResultChange::Same=>{},

  191	        let new_domains=crate::result_domains::signature(after,new);
  192	        // A domain introduced only for a newly returned field is covered by

  194	        let changed:Vec<_>=old_domains.keys().collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>().into_iter().filter(|key|old_domains.get(*key)!=new_domains.get(*key)).cloned().collect();
  195	        if !changed.is_empty() {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: declared source domains consumed by this operation changed: {}; results or refusals may change even when the TypeScript type stays number/string; preserve the old domains or verify old-client handling",changed.join(", ")));}
  196	        if refusals(before)!=refusals(after) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: BEHAVIOR REVIEW: refusal codes/messages changed ({:?} → {:?}); verify intended denials separately from input breaks",refusals(before),refusals(after)));}
  197	    }
  198	    lines
  199	}

  201	/// Human result advice groups source columns across operations. JSON keeps compare().
  202	pub fn compact(lines:&[String])->Vec<String>{
  203	    use std::collections::BTreeSet;
  204	    let mut out=Vec::new();let mut groups=BTreeMap::<String,BTreeSet<String>>::new();
  205	    for line in lines {
  206	        let Some((prefix,detail))=line.split_once(": RESULT REVIEW: ") else {out.push(line.clone());continue};
  207	        let operation=prefix.rsplit_once("operation ").map(|(_,name)|name).unwrap_or("unknown");
  208	        if let Some((_,columns))=detail.split_once("declared source domains consumed by this operation changed: ") {
  209	            for column in columns.split(';').next().unwrap_or(columns).split(", "){groups.entry(column.into()).or_default().insert(operation.into());}
  210	        }else{groups.entry(detail.into()).or_default().insert(operation.into());}
  211	    }
  212	    for(detail,ops)in groups{out.push(format!("old-client compatibility: RESULT REVIEW: {detail}; operations [{}]; verify old-client handling (full per-operation evidence in --json)",ops.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")));}
  213	    out
  214	}

//! A process-local clock for development and explicitly classified staging stores.
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — preserve expiry tests and tell callers how to recover.
pub(crate) const SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Time travel also advances session expiry and unplaced-upload collection: seven-day password sessions may now be expired. Sign in again after the jump and upload unplaced bytes after it; never replay an ambiguous clock advance.";

pub(crate) const PRESERVED_SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Authenticated development and staging sessions keep their remaining lifetime across this jump; sessions:expire explicitly tests credential expiry. Unplaced uploads still age. Never replay an ambiguous advance.";

const MAX_TIME: i64 = snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX;

pub fn input(message: impl Into<String>) -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INPUT", "clock", message).guide("clock") }
pub fn release() -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY", "clock", "clock controls require dev or a deploy --staging store; production always uses wall time").guide("clock") }

/// Isolated time tests stay inside an assigned range, or request a free port.
pub(crate) fn isolated_command() -> String {
    isolated_range(std::env::var("PORT_LO").ok().as_deref(), std::env::var("PORT_HI").ok().as_deref())
}
fn isolated_range(lo: Option<&str>, hi: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match (lo.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok()), hi.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())) {
        (Some(lo), Some(hi)) if lo > 0 && hi >= lo => format!("dev --memory --port {lo}-{hi} within the current range"),
        _ => "dev --memory --port 0".into(),
    }
}

pub fn duration(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if text.starts_with('-') { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
    let text = text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text);
    let split = text.bytes().position(|b| !b.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(text.len());
    let (number, unit) = text.split_at(split);
    let multiplier = match unit { "ms" => 1, "s" => 1_000, "m" => 60_000, "h" => 3_600_000, "d" => 86_400_000, "w" => 604_800_000, _ => 0 };
    number.parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(multiplier)).filter(|n| *n > 0 && *n <= MAX_TIME)
        .ok_or_else(|| input("expected a positive whole duration with ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as +25h"))
}

pub fn offset(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if let Some(rest) = text.strip_prefix('-') { duration(rest).map(|n| -n) } else { duration(text) }
}

fn time(value: Option<i64>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    value.filter(|n| (0..=MAX_TIME).contains(n)).ok_or_else(|| input("time must be Unix milliseconds in 0..9007199254740991; choose a smaller time or duration"))
}

pub fn run_now(text: Option<&String>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    let now = snapback4_core::now_ms();
    match text {
        None => Ok(now),
        Some(text) if text.starts_with('+') => time(now.checked_add(duration(text)?)),
        Some(text) => time(text.parse().ok()),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Clock {
    dev: bool,
    base: i64,
    offset: i64,
    started: Instant,
    epoch: String,
    revision: u64,
    #[cfg(test)]
    frozen: bool,
}

impl Clock {
    pub fn new(dev: bool, offset: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        if !dev && offset != 0 { return Err(release()); }
        Ok(Self { dev, offset, base: time(snapback4_core::now_ms().checked_add(offset))?, started: Instant::now(),
            epoch: snapback4_core::ids::mint(snapback4_core::now_ms(), &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?, revision: 0, #[cfg(test)] frozen: false })
    }
    pub fn staging(offset: i64, floor: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        let mut clock = Self::new(true, offset)?;
        let delta = floor.saturating_sub(clock.now()).max(0);
        if delta > 0 { clock.advance(delta)?; }
        Ok(clock)
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn freeze(&mut self, now: i64) { self.base = now; self.frozen = true; }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        #[cfg(test)] if self.frozen { return self.base; }
        if !self.dev { return snapback4_core::now_ms(); }
        self.base.saturating_add(self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64).min(MAX_TIME)
    }
    /// Identifies samples taken before/after a restart or deliberate clock jump.
    pub fn offset(&self) -> i64 { self.offset }
    pub fn revision(&self) -> String { format!("{}:{}", self.epoch, self.revision) }
    pub fn presence_now(&self) -> i64 {
        // Production grace is elapsed real time, unaffected by wall-clock corrections.
        if self.dev { self.now() } else { self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64 }
    }
    /// Back to wall time: the offset `--clock-offset` and every advance added
    /// is dropped (a development reset's `{"clock":"reset"}`).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = 0;
        self.base = snapback4_core::now_ms();
        self.started = Instant::now();
        #[cfg(test)] { self.frozen = false; }
        Ok(self.base)
    }
    pub fn advance(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        if milliseconds <= 0 { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
        let next = time(self.now().checked_add(milliseconds))?;
        let offset = self.offset.checked_add(milliseconds).ok_or_else(|| input("cumulative clock offset overflow"))?;
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = offset;
        self.base = next;
        self.started = Instant::now();
        Ok(next)
    }
}

/// The control CLI only talks to a loopback dev host. It does not open its store.
pub fn command(options: &crate::verbs::Options) -> i32 {
    let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
        let draining = options.positionals == ["drain"];
        if !draining && (options.positionals.len() != 2 || options.positionals[0] != "advance") {
            return Err(input(format!("usage: {}", crate::cli_flags::synopsis("clock"))).to_string());
        }
        let duration_text = if draining { "0ms" } else { options.positionals[1].as_str() };
        if !draining { duration(duration_text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; }
        let release_path = options.flags.get("release").map(|dir| std::path::PathBuf::from(dir).join("store.sqlite"));
        if release_path.is_some() && options.flags.contains_key("port") { return Err("clock --release does not accept --port".into()); }
        let (address, instance, token) = if let Some(path) = &release_path {
            let store = snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::open_read_only(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if store.deployment_environment().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(release().to_string()); }
            let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(path).ok_or("staging clock requires a running serve")?;
            let session = crate::serve::token::mint_live(path, "clock", 1).map_err(|(_,error)|error)?;
            (address,None,Some(session.token))
        } else {
            let (address,instance)=crate::verbs::dev_address(options)?;
            // A production listener has no development-token registry entry.
            // Ask its read-only clock door first so the CLI preserves the
            // server's actionable refusal instead of failing token discovery.
            if let Ok((_, status)) = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/clock/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5))
                && status["denied"]["code"] == "E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY"
            {
                return Err(release().to_string());
            }
            let token=crate::verbs::mint_for_dev(address,"operator",1)?;
            (address,instance,Some(token))
        };
        let mut body = serde_json::json!({"duration":duration_text,"eachBoundary":options.flags.contains_key("each-boundary"), "drain":!options.flags.contains_key("no-drain"), "allowHeld":options.flags.contains_key("allow-held")});
        if options.flags.contains_key("expire-sessions") { body["sessions"] = "expire".into(); }
        if draining && options.flags.contains_key("no-drain") { return Err(input("clock drain does not accept --no-drain").to_string()); }
        let body = body.to_string();
        // The common HTTP/1.0 exchange is EOF-delimited and bounds replies at
        // 64 MiB, enough for the preflight's complete explicit window report.
        let response = if release_path.is_some() {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_authorized(address,"POST","/dev/clock/advance",None,token.as_deref(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        } else {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_dev_authorized(address,"/dev/clock/advance",instance.as_deref(),token.as_deref().unwrap(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        };
        let (status, json) = response.map_err(|error| {
            let evidence = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5)).ok()
                .map(|(_, status)| format!("now={}, skewMs={}", status["now"], status["skewMs"]))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "clock status unavailable".into());
            format!("clock advance reply failed at {address}: {error}; time may already have advanced ({evidence}); inspect /dev/status and queued work before retrying; for an isolated dev pass --port N")
        })?;
        if let Some(notice) = json["sessionNotice"].as_str() { eprintln!("clock: {notice}"); }
        if let Some(held) = json["held"].as_array() {
            for schedule in held.iter().filter(|s| s["holdCode"] == "saved-boundary") {
                eprintln!("clock: schedule {}: {}", schedule["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"), schedule["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or("held"));
            }
        }
        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
            if json.get("now").is_some() {
                eprintln!("clock: incomplete advance report (time already moved): {}", serde_json::json!({"now":json["now"],"fired":json["fired"],"held":json["held"]}));
            }
            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
        }
        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
        Ok(json.to_string())
    })();
    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
}

//! Development doors beside the operation routes: `POST /seed`, `POST /dev/reset`, and the
//! `--no-watch` hint that names a schema edited on disk after adoption.
use super::{Shared, lock, refusal_json, respond_timed};
use crate::project::{Project, SourceStamp};
use serde_json::{Value as Json, json};
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use snapback4_core::wire;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Mutex;
use tiny_http::Request;

/// The source stamp each `--no-watch` dev host adopted, by project root.
static PINNED: Mutex<BTreeMap<PathBuf, SourceStamp>> = Mutex::new(BTreeMap::new());

pub(super) fn closed() -> Refusal {
    Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "development doors are closed; use serve staging with real users (guide staging), or explicitly opt into dev --unsafe-dev-doors for local fixtures").guide("staging")
}

pub(super) fn pin(project: &Path, stamp: SourceStamp) {
    PINNED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).insert(project.to_owned(), stamp);
}

/// A `--no-watch` host serves the schema it started with. When a request
/// names an operation or argument that host does not know and the `.q` files
/// changed on disk since, say so: the edit is real, it was just never adopted.
pub(super) fn stale(shared: &Shared, refusal: Refusal) -> Refusal {
    let Some(adopted) = PINNED.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).get(&shared.project).copied() else { return refusal };
    if (Project { root: shared.project.clone() }).sources_stamp() == adopted { return refusal; }
    let message = format!("{}; this dev host runs with --no-watch and snapback/ changed on disk after it adopted its schema, so the edit is not served", refusal.message);
    Refusal { message, rewrite: Some("restart `snapback4 dev` (or drop --no-watch so saves re-adopt), then retry".into()), ..refusal }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#8 — persona names are not their principals; dev only.
pub(super) fn persona_argument(shared: &Shared, kinds: &BTreeMap<String,snapback4_core::ir::ArgType>, args: &Json) -> Option<Refusal> {
    if !shared.personas { return None; }
    let bound = lock(&shared.bound);
    crate::persona_principals::arguments(&bound.personas,kinds,args)
}
// Rows are written as the system principal; each names its id because seed is an upsert by id.
pub(super) fn seed(request: Request, shared: &Shared, body: &str) {
    if !shared.dev_doors() || !request.remote_addr().is_some_and(|a| a.ip().is_loopback()) {
        respond_timed(request, shared, 403, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "seeding is a development door")) }));
        return;
    }
    let refuse = |request, refusal: Refusal| respond_timed(request, shared, 400, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&refusal.guide("personas")) }));
    let rows: Vec<Json> = match serde_json::from_str(body) {
        Ok(Json::Array(rows)) => rows,
        _ => return refuse(request, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "seed takes a JSON array of {table, row}")),
    };
    let outcome = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
        shared.dev_authority(engine).map_err(|why| (403, why))?;
        let now = shared.now();
        let typed = typed_rows(engine.schema(), &rows, now).map_err(|why| (400, why.guide("personas")))?;
        let count = engine.seed_at(typed, now).map_err(|error| (200, seed_refusal(error)))?;
        shared.durable_committed(engine);
        Ok::<_, (u16, Refusal)>(count)
    });
    match outcome {
        Ok(count) => respond_timed(request, shared, 200, json!({"seeded":count})),
        Err((status, why)) => respond_timed(request, shared, status, json!({"denied":why})),
    }

}

/// `/seed` rows checked against the served schema and typed, or the first problem.
fn typed_rows(schema: &snapback4_core::Schema, rows: &[Json], now: i64) -> Result<Vec<(String, snapback4_core::Value)>, Refusal> {
    let mut typed = Vec::new();
    for (index, entry) in rows.iter().enumerate() {
        let (Some(table), Some(row)) = (entry.get("table").and_then(Json::as_str), entry.get("row")) else {
            return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", "each seed entry is {table, row}"));
        };
        let Some(definition) = schema.table(table) else {
            return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("unknown table {table}")));
        };
        if row.is_object() && row.get("id").is_none_or(|id| !id.is_string()) {
            return Err(missing_id(index, table));
        }
        let mut row = row.clone();
        crate::verbs::test_fixture::relative_times(definition, &mut row, now)
            .map_err(|why| Refusal::new("E_FIXTURE_TIME", "input", format!("seed row {index} ({table}): {why}")))?;
        if let Some(why) = wire::bare_principal(definition, &row) {
            return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("seed row {index} ({table}): {why}")));
        }
        match wire::row_from_json(definition, &row) {
            Ok(value) => typed.push((table.to_owned(), value)),
            Err(why) => return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("{table}: {why}"))),
        }
    }
    Ok(typed)
}

fn seed_refusal(error: snapback4_core::RuntimeError) -> Refusal {
    let mut refusal = error.refusal();
    // Reseeding with changed immutable values reads like a rule problem; say what happened.
    if refusal.code == "E_CONSTRAINT" && refusal.message.ends_with(" is immutable") {
        refusal.message.push_str("; /seed is an upsert by id, and a row with that id already exists with a different value in that column. Reseed it with its original value, give the row a new id, POST /dev/reset first, or restart dev with --memory for an empty store");
    }
    refusal
}

/// What `POST /dev/reset` was asked to do: the body is empty, a `/seed`
/// array, or `{"seed": [..], "clock": "reset"}` with either key optional.
#[derive(Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
struct ResetRequest { seed: Vec<Json>, clock: bool }

fn reset_request(body: &str) -> Result<ResetRequest, Refusal> {
    const SHAPE: &str = "reset takes no body, a /seed array [{table, row}, ..], or {\"seed\": [..], \"clock\": \"reset\"} with either key optional";
    if body.trim().is_empty() { return Ok(ResetRequest::default()); }
    match serde_json::from_str(body) {
        Ok(Json::Array(seed)) => Ok(ResetRequest { seed, clock: false }),
        Ok(Json::Object(fields)) => {
            let mut request = ResetRequest::default();
            for (key, value) in fields {
                match (key.as_str(), value) {
                    ("seed", Json::Array(seed)) => request.seed = seed,
                    ("clock", Json::String(clock)) if clock == "reset" => request.clock = true,
                    ("clock", Json::String(clock)) if clock == "keep" => request.clock = false,
                    ("clock", other) => return Err(crate::dev_clock::input(format!("reset's clock is \"reset\" (back to wall time) or \"keep\" (the default), not {other}"))),
                    (key, _) => return Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("{SHAPE}; got key {key:?}"))),
                }
            }
            Ok(request)
        }
        _ => Err(Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", SHAPE)),
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.25 — one transaction: empty, new identity, reseed; then the host's caches follow.
pub(super) fn reset(request: Request, shared: &Shared, body: &str) {
    if !shared.dev_doors() || !request.remote_addr().is_some_and(|a| a.ip().is_loopback()) {
        respond_timed(request, shared, 403, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&reset_release()) }));
        return;
    }
    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
    let refuse = |request, refusal: Refusal| respond_timed(request, shared, 400, json!({ "denied": refusal_json(&refusal.guide("testing")) }));
    let asked = match reset_request(body) {
        Ok(asked) => asked,
        Err(refusal) => return refuse(request, refusal),
    };
    // Serialize with clock advances, then take the engine before the clock:
    // the order clock advance and worker claims use.
    let advance = lock(&shared.maintenance).advance.clone();
    let _advance = lock(&advance);
    let result = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {

    shared.dev_authority(engine).map_err(|why| (403, why))?;
    let mut clock = lock(&shared.clock).clone();
    if asked.clock { clock.reset().map_err(|why| (400, why))?; }
    let now = clock.now();
    // Resolve against the prospective reset clock before changing any durable state.
    let typed = typed_rows(engine.schema(), &asked.seed, now).map_err(|why| (400, why))?;
    let reset = engine.dev_reset_at(typed, now).map_err(|error| (200, seed_refusal(error)))?;
    if asked.clock { *lock(&shared.clock) = clock; }
    *lock(&shared.dev_reset_store) = Some(reset.store_id.clone());
    // The reset committed a new identity and a new authority clock. Replace,
    // rather than max with, the retired store's cached high-water mark.
    shared.time_audience_clock.store(if engine.schema().tables.values().any(|t| t.not_before.is_some()) { now } else { i64::MIN }, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
    // Detached readers reopen; the following registry, change answers and
    // `/dev/status` forget the old identity. Wake then names the new store,
    // so every held poll returns and each client sees the replacement.
    let sites = lock(&shared.bound).refusal_sites.clone();
    lock(&shared.readers).replace(engine, &sites);
    lock(&shared.adoption).store_id = reset.store_id.clone();
    if let Ok(reader) = snapback4_core::engine::following_history::Reader::new() { *lock(&shared.following) = reader; }
    *lock(&shared.change_answers) = Default::default();
    shared.durable_committed(engine);
    let generation = engine.generation();
    Ok::<_, (u16, Refusal)>((reset, generation))
    });
    let (reset, generation) = match result {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err((status, why)) => return respond_timed(request, shared, status, json!({"denied":why})),
    };
    let assets = reset.assets.len();
    if let Err(error) = reset.assets.remove_files() { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4 dev: reset left asset bytes behind: {error}"); }
    let now = shared.now();
    snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4 dev: store reset (store {} → {}, seeded {}) in {} ms", reset.previous_store_id, reset.store_id, reset.seeded, started.elapsed().as_millis());
    respond_timed(request, shared, 200, json!({
        "sessionNotice":"Reset replaced the store and removed its accounts and sessions. Discard cached credentials/localStorage for this backend, sign up again and reprovision roles; use a fresh memory host per independent proof.",
        "reset": true, "seeded": reset.seeded, "generation": generation, "storeId": reset.store_id,
        "previousStoreId": reset.previous_store_id, "head": reset.seq, "assetsRemoved": assets,
        "now": now, "clockOffsetMs": lock(&shared.clock).offset(), "skewMs": now - snapback4_core::now_ms(), "ms": started.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,
    }));
}

pub(super) fn reset_release() -> Refusal {
    Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "resetting the store is a development door; snapback4 serve never empties a store")
        .guide("testing")
}

fn missing_id(index: usize, table: &str) -> Refusal {
    Refusal::new("E_FIELD", "input", format!(
        "missing field id: seed row {index} ({table}) has no string id. /seed is an upsert by id, so every row names its own; \
         rerunning the same seed then updates those rows instead of duplicating them"))
        .rewrite("give each row a 26-character id in Crockford base32 (digits and capital letters except I, L, O, U), \
                  e.g. \"row\": {\"id\": \"0000000000000000000000SEED\", ..}; in JavaScript `idFrom(\"seed:alice\")` from \
                  snapback4/client derives the same valid id from a label every time, and a reference column takes that id")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    #[test]
    fn the_missing_id_example_is_a_valid_id() {
        let refusal = super::missing_id(0, "notes");
        let rewrite = refusal.rewrite.unwrap();
        let example = rewrite.split("\"id\": \"").nth(1).unwrap().split('"').next().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(example.len(), 26, "{example}");
        assert!(snapback4_core::ids::minted_at(example).is_some(), "{example} is Crockford base32");
        assert!(refusal.message.starts_with("missing field id"), "{}", refusal.message);
    }
}

//! Exact service principals named by compiled authorization facts.
use snapback4_core::{
    Value,
    ir::{BinaryOp, Expr, Input, Stmt},
    schema::{RuleExpr, RuleTerm},
};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

fn principal(value: &Value) -> Option<&str> {
    match value {
        Value::Id(value) => value
            .strip_prefix("service:")
            .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
            .map(|_| value.as_str()),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn rule(rule: &RuleExpr, seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>, positive: bool) {
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Viewer, RuleTerm::Literal(value))
        | RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Literal(value), RuleTerm::Viewer)
            if positive =>
        {
            if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
                seats.insert(value.into());
            }
        }
        RuleExpr::And(rules) | RuleExpr::Or(rules) => rules
            .iter()
            .for_each(|rule| self::rule(rule, seats, positive)),
        RuleExpr::Not(rule) => self::rule(rule, seats, !positive),
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn expression(expr: &Expr, seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>, positive: bool) {
    match expr {
        Expr::Binary {
            op: BinaryOp::Eq | BinaryOp::SameValueZero,
            left,
            right,
        } => match (&**left, &**right, positive) {
            (Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), Expr::Literal(value), true)
            | (Expr::Literal(value), Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), true) => {
                if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
                    seats.insert(value.into());
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        },
        Expr::Binary {
            op: BinaryOp::And | BinaryOp::Or,
            left,
            right,
        } => {
            expression(left, seats, positive);
            expression(right, seats, positive);
        }
        Expr::Unary {
            op: snapback4_core::ir::UnaryOp::Not,
            value,
        } => expression(value, seats, !positive),
        Expr::Block { body, value } => {
            statements(body, seats);
            expression(value, seats, positive);
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn statements(body: &[Stmt], seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {
    for statement in body {
        match statement {
            Stmt::Require { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
            Stmt::If {
                then_body,
                else_body,
                ..
            } => {
                statements(then_body, seats);
                statements(else_body, seats);
            }
            Stmt::For { body, .. } => statements(body, seats),
            Stmt::Check { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
            Stmt::WriteTarget {
                condition: Some(condition),
                ..
            } => statements(&condition.setup, seats),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — minted seats stay ordinary principals; this is advisory schema evidence, never a grant.
pub(crate) fn collect(bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    let mut seats = BTreeSet::new();
    for table in bound.schema.tables.values() {
        for rule in [
            &table.rules.read,
            &table.rules.insert,
            &table.rules.update,
            &table.rules.delete,
        ] {
            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
        }
        for rule in table.column_reads.values() {
            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
        }
    }
    for program in &bound.programs {
        statements(&program.program.body, &mut seats);
    }
    seats.extend(
        bound
            .schema
            .schedules
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|schedule| schedule.service.clone()),
    );
    seats.extend(
        bound
            .schema
            .routes
            .values()
            .filter_map(|route| route.service.clone()),
    );
    seats
}

    }

   156	    let mut chunks = 0;
   157	    while drain || chunks < 500 {
   158	        if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { break; }
   159	        if phase(shared, engine_work(shared, move |engine, budget, shared| engine.run_timeline_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget)), drain, "timeline delivery")?.is_none() { break; }
   160	        chunks += 1;
   161	    }
   162	    Ok(chunks)
   163	}
   164	
   165	// @ref LLP 3000#contended-read-serving — ordinary-priority bulk work yields
   166	// outside every shared lock. Aged service protects finite backlogs from traffic.
   167	const BULK_AGE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
   168	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   169	enum BulkKind { Delivery, Recount, Job }
   170	pub(super) struct State {
   171	    next: BulkKind,
   172	    serviced: Instant,
   173	    resume_at: Instant,
   174	    empty_pause: Duration,
   175	    advancing: bool,
   176	    // Explicit mutation-boundary tests pause all background maintenance until drain.
   177	    paused: bool,
   178	    // Separate clock callers (and a dev reset) may wait here; maintenance never takes this lock.
   179	    pub(super) advance: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<()>>,
   180	    #[cfg(test)]
   181	    lose_advance_ack: bool,
   182	}
   183	impl Default for State {
   184	    fn default() -> Self {
   185	        let now = Instant::now();
   186	        Self { next: BulkKind::Delivery, serviced: now, resume_at: now, empty_pause: Duration::ZERO,
   187	            advancing: false, paused: false, advance: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(())),
   188	            #[cfg(test)] lose_advance_ack: false }
   189	    }
   190	}
   191	impl State {
   192	    pub(super) fn with_pause(paused: bool) -> Self { Self { paused, ..Self::default() } }
   193	    fn aged(&self, now: Instant) -> bool { now.saturating_duration_since(self.serviced) >= BULK_AGE }
   194	    fn eligible(&self, now: Instant, aged_only: bool) -> bool {
   195	        !self.advancing && !self.paused && if aged_only { self.aged(now) } else { now >= self.resume_at }
   196	    }
   197	    fn completed(&mut self, now: Instant, elapsed: Duration, contended: bool, worked: bool) {
   198	        self.next = match self.next { BulkKind::Delivery => BulkKind::Recount, BulkKind::Recount => BulkKind::Job, BulkKind::Job => BulkKind::Delivery };
   199	        self.serviced = now;
   200	        // Target 1/8 CPU duty under contention, charging consumed thread CPU,
   201	        // including atomic overruns. Cap at 100 ms; aged service is independent.
   202	        let cap = Duration::from_millis(100);
   203	        let charged = if contended { (elapsed * 7).min(cap) } else { Duration::ZERO };
   204	        self.empty_pause += charged;
   205	        // @ref LLP 3000#contended-read-serving — empty kinds keep their CPU
   206	        // charge, but repay it with the next useful slice or the empty cycle.
   207	        // Avoid two extra scheduler wakeups for every single delivery slice.
   208	        let pause = if worked || self.empty_pause >= cap { self.empty_pause.min(cap) } else { Duration::ZERO };
   209	        self.empty_pause -= pause;
   210	        // An aged slice can finish after bulk flushes empty-cycle debt. Append
   211	        // this charge without discarding repayment still owed in that ordering.
   212	        self.resume_at = self.resume_at.max(now) + pause;
   213	    }
   214	
   215	    fn empty_cycle(&mut self, now: Instant) -> Duration {
   216	        let pause = std::mem::take(&mut self.empty_pause);
   217	        // A timed worker may just have scheduled repayment. Append remaining
   218	        // debt rather than overlapping (and losing) either charge.
   219	        self.resume_at = self.resume_at.max(now) + pause;
   220	        self.resume_at.saturating_duration_since(now)
   221	    }
   222	}
   223	
   224	// Admission owns no maintenance gate. Once admitted, the engine serializes the
   225	// cursor's read -> chunk commit -> advance; the gate only protects small state
   226	// accesses. Ordinary work never waits for a bulk thread to enter the engine.
   227	fn bulk_slice(shared: &Shared, aged_only: bool) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   228	    if !lock(&shared.maintenance).eligible(Instant::now(), aged_only) { return Ok(false); }
   229	    engine_work(shared, move |engine, budget, shared| {
   230	        let kind = {
   231	            let state = lock(&shared.maintenance);
   232	            if !state.eligible(Instant::now(), aged_only) { return Ok(false); }
   233	            state.next
   234	        };
   235	        let started = SliceClock::start();
   236	        let result = match kind {
   237	            BulkKind::Delivery => engine.run_timeline_turn_for(shared.now(), budget).map(|r| r.is_some()),
   238	            BulkKind::Recount => engine.run_view_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget).map(|r| r.is_some()),
   239	            BulkKind::Job => {
   240	                let run = engine.run_job_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget);
   241	                for line in engine.take_native_logs() { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: native {line}"); }
   242	                run.map(|run| {
   243	                    if let Some(run) = &run {
   244	                        match run.state {
   245	                            snapback4_core::JobState::Done => snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: job {} done: {} chunks, {} rows written", run.name, run.chunks, run.rows_written),
   246	                            snapback4_core::JobState::Parked => {
   247	                                if shared.personas { shared.refusals.job(run); }
   248	                                snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: job {} parked after {} chunks: {}", run.name, run.chunks, run.error.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
   249	                            }
   250	                            _ => {}
   251	                        }
   252	                    }
   253	                    run.is_some()
   254	                })
   255	            }
   256	        };
   257	        lock(&shared.maintenance).completed(Instant::now(), started.consumed(), budget == CONTENDED_TIME || shared.engine.has_waiters(), result.as_ref().map_or(true, |worked| *worked));
   258	        result
   259	    })
   260	}
   261	
   262	fn timely_engine_work<T: Default + Send + 'static>(shared: &Shared, run: impl FnOnce(&mut snapback4_core::Engine, Duration, &Shared) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> + Send + 'static) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   263	    let result = engine_work(shared, move |engine, budget, shared| {
   264	        if { let state = lock(&shared.maintenance); state.advancing || state.paused } { return Ok(T::default()); }
   265	        run(engine, budget, shared)
   266	    });
   267	    promote_aged(shared, Instant::now());
   268	    result
   269	}
   270	
   271	fn timely(shared: &Shared, tick: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   272	    phase(shared, timely_engine_work(shared, move |engine, budget, shared| engine.sweep_expired_for(shared.now(), 2_000, budget)), false, "the expiry sweep")?;
   273	    if !shared.hold_schedules {
   274	        let count = timely_engine_work(shared, move |engine, _, _| Ok(engine.schema().schedules.len()))?;
   275	        for index in 0..count {
   276	            // One atomic boundary per admission, never the entire schedule set.
   277	            // Adoption between slices is harmless: the next tick visits its set.
   278	            let fired = phase(shared, timely_engine_work(shared, move |engine, _, shared| engine.fire_schedule_at(shared.now(), index)), false, "schedules")?;
   279	            for name in fired { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: schedule {name} fired"); }
   280	        }
   281	    }
   282	    if tick % 5 == 0 {
   283	        phase(shared, timely_engine_work(shared, move |engine, budget, shared| {
   284	            let result = engine.requeue_expired_actions_for(shared.now(), budget);
   285	            if result.as_ref().is_ok_and(|n| *n > 0) { shared.durable_committed(engine); }
   286	            result
   287	        }), false, "the action lease sweep")?;
   288	        let effects = phase(shared, timely_engine_work(shared, move |engine, budget, shared| {
   289	            let result = engine.requeue_expired_effects_for(shared.now(), budget);
   290	            if result.as_ref().is_ok_and(|n| *n > 0) { shared.durable_committed(engine); }
   291	            result
   292	        }), false, "the effect lease sweep")?;
   293	        if effects > 0 { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: {effects} effect leases expired; queued again"); }
   294	    }
   295	    if tick % 60 == 0 {
   296	        phase(shared, (|| {
   297	            let Some(mut sweep) = timely_engine_work(shared, move |engine, budget, shared| engine.prepare_asset_sweep_for(shared.now(), budget).map(Some))? else { return Ok(()); };
   298	            // Bounded stale batch; filesystem work owns no engine lock.
   299	            sweep.remove_files()?;
   300	            while !sweep.is_empty() {
   301	                // A clock drain that began between file removal and retirement
   302	                // owns the sweep now. Its durable metadata also permits retry
   303	                // on the next asset tick; do not spin on skipped slices.
   304	                let Some((finished, next)) = timely_engine_work(shared, move |engine, budget, _| engine.finish_asset_sweep_for(&mut sweep, budget).map(|finished| Some((finished, sweep))))? else { break; };
   305	                sweep = next;
   306	                if finished == 0 { break; }
   307	            }
   308	            Ok(())
   309	        })(), false, "the asset sweep")?;
   310	    }
   311	    Ok(())
   312	}
   313	
   314	pub(super) fn maintain(shared: Arc<Shared>) {
   315	    let mut tick = 0;
   316	    let mut last_tick = Instant::now();
   317	    loop {
   318	        if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { return; }
   319	        {
   320	            let state = lock(&shared.maintenance);
   321	            if !state.advancing && !state.paused && let Err(error) = shared.ephemeral.sweep(shared.now()) { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: ephemeral sweep: {error}"); }
   322	        }
   323	        if last_tick.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(1) {
   324	            tick += 1; last_tick = Instant::now();
   325	            // One bounded reclamation slice; abandoned bytes remain charged
   326	            // until their actual records are dropped. No engine lock is held.
   327	            lock(&shared.following).reclaim(shared.now(), snapback4_core::Ceilings { heap_bytes: 1 << 20, ..Default::default() });
   328	            if let Err(error) = timely(&shared, tick) { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: maintenance failed: {error}"); }
   329	        }
   330	        promote_aged(&shared, Instant::now());
   331	        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
   332	    }
   333	}
   334	
   335	fn promote_aged(shared: &Shared, now: Instant) {
   336	    if lock(&shared.maintenance).eligible(now, true) {
   337	        if let Err(error) = bulk_slice(shared, true) { super::adoption::background_failure(shared, "aged bulk maintenance", &error); }
   338	    }
   339	}
   340	
   341	pub(super) fn bulk(shared: Arc<Shared>) {
   342	    loop {
   343	        if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { return; }
   344	        let observed = *lock(&shared.seq);
   345	        let mut did_work = false;
   346	        for _ in 0..3 {
   347	            if crate::lifecycle::stopping() { return; }
   348	            match bulk_slice(&shared, false) {
   349	                Ok(worked) => did_work |= worked,
   350	                Err(error) => {
   351	                    super::adoption::background_failure(&shared, "bulk maintenance admission", &error);
   352	                    // Refusal is not an idle slice: preserve the due scheduler
   353	                    // and retry on the next bounded turn, with a logged reason.
   354	                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
   355	                    did_work = true;
   356	                    break;
   357	                }
   358	            }
   359	            let pause = lock(&shared.maintenance).resume_at.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now());
   360	            if !pause.is_zero() {
   361	                // No shared lock survives this pause. Request commits do not
   362	                // cancel repayment; empty kinds do not idle an active cycle.
   363	                std::thread::sleep(pause.min(Duration::from_millis(100)));
   364	            }
   365	        }
   366	        if !did_work {
   367	            loop {
   368	                let pause = lock(&shared.maintenance).empty_cycle(Instant::now());
   369	                if pause.is_zero() { break; }
   370	                std::thread::sleep(pause.min(Duration::from_millis(100)));
   371	            }
   372	            let seq = lock(&shared.seq);
   373	            if *seq == observed {
   374	                drop(shared.committed.wait_timeout(seq, Duration::from_millis(100)).unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()));
   375	            }
   376	        }
   377	    }
   378	}

   380	// Reset even when a debug/unwind request panics mid-drain. Engine poison
   381	// recovery and durable work cursors retain the normal retry semantics.
   382	struct Advancing<'a>(&'a Shared);
   383	impl Drop for Advancing<'_> {
   384	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   385	        let mut state = lock(&self.0.maintenance);
   386	        state.advancing = false;
   387	        state.next = BulkKind::Delivery;
   388	    }
   389	}
   390	
   391	fn completed_drain(work: Work, stopping: bool) -> Result<Work, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
   392	    if stopping {
   393	        return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INTERRUPTED", "clock", "clock advanced, but host shutdown interrupted the drain; inspect queued work instead of repeating the advance").guide("clock"));
   394	    }
   395	    Ok(work)
   396	}

   402	fn clock_service(request: &Request, shared: &Shared) -> Result<Option<String>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
   403	    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — real-user dev clock authority is independent of fixture doors.
   404	    if shared.personas {
   405	        match super::session_identity::principal_of(request,shared) {
   406	            Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind == "service" && principal == "service:operator" => return Ok(Some(principal)),
   407	            _ if shared.dev_doors() && crate::auth::bearer_token(request).is_err() => return Ok(None),
   408	            _ => return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "development clock control requires a full service:operator token").guide("clock")),
   409	        }
   410	    }
   411	    if !staging(shared)? { return Err(crate::dev_clock::release()); }
   412	    match super::session_identity::principal_of(request,shared) {
   413	        Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind == "service" && principal.starts_with("service:") => Ok(Some(principal)),
   414	        _ => Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_AUTH", "auth", "staging clock control requires a full service token").guide("clock")),
   415	    }
   416	}
   417	fn checkpoint_clock(engine: &mut snapback4_core::Engine, delta: i64, before: i64, preserve: bool, checkpoint: &snapback4_core::metadata::StagingClock) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   418	    let result = engine.checkpoint_staging_clock_at(delta, before, preserve, checkpoint);
   419	    #[cfg(feature = "postgres")]
   420	    if matches!(result, Err(RuntimeError::CommitOutcomeUnknown(_))) { crate::lifecycle::uncertain_clock_commit(); }
   421	    result
   422	}
   423	fn incomplete_report(cause: &snapback4_core::Refusal) -> snapback4_core::Refusal {

   425	        format!("clock already advanced; report incomplete ({cause}); inspect clock or use clock drain (0ms); do not replay the advance"))
   426	        .guide("clock")

   428	fn advance_error(error: &snapback4_core::Refusal, published: Option<i64>, milliseconds: i64) -> (u16, serde_json::Value) {
   429	    match published {
   430	        Some(now) => (500, json!({"now":now,"advancedMs":milliseconds,"reportIncomplete":true,"denied":incomplete_report(error)})),
   431	        None => (refusal_status(error, 400), json!({"denied":refusal_json(error)})),
   432	    }
   433	}

   435	pub(super) fn advance(request: Request, shared: &Shared, body: &str) {
   436	    let service = match clock_service(&request, shared) {
   437	        Ok(service) => service,
   438	        Err(why) => return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&why)})),
   439	    };
   440	    let payload = match serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(body) {
   441	        Ok(payload) => payload,
   442	        Err(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))})),
   443	    };
   444	    let each_boundary = match payload.get("eachBoundary") {
   445	        None => false,
   446	        Some(serde_json::Value::Bool(value)) => *value,
   447	        Some(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("eachBoundary must be a boolean"))})),
   448	    };
   449	    let boolean = |key: &str, default: bool| -> Result<bool, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
   450	        match payload.get(key) {
   451	            None => Ok(default), Some(serde_json::Value::Bool(value)) => Ok(*value),
   452	            Some(_) => Err(crate::dev_clock::input(format!("{key} must be a boolean"))),
   453	        }
   454	    };
   455	    let (drain, allow_held) = match boolean("drain", true).and_then(|drain| Ok((drain, boolean("allowHeld", false)?))) {
   456	        Ok(options) => options,
   457	        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
   458	    };
   459	    if each_boundary && !drain { return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("eachBoundary requires drain:true"))})); }
   460	    let preserve_sessions = match payload.get("sessions").and_then(|s| s.as_str()) {
   461	        None if payload.get("sessions").is_none() => service.is_some(),
   462	        Some("preserve") if service.is_some() => true,
   463	        Some("expire") => false,
   464	        _ => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("sessions must be preserve (authenticated development or staging only) or expire"))})),
   465	    };
   466	    let duration = payload.get("duration").and_then(|value| value.as_str());
   467	    let milliseconds = match duration.ok_or_else(|| crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))
   468	        .and_then(|duration| if duration == "0ms" && drain { Ok(0) } else { crate::dev_clock::duration(duration) }) {
   469	        Ok(milliseconds) => milliseconds,
   470	        Err(error) => return respond(request, refusal_status(&error, 400), json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
   471	    };
   472	    // Serialize clock callers only. Background slices check advancing after
   473	    // engine admission and skip during this synchronous drain.
   474	    let advance = lock(&shared.maintenance).advance.clone();
   475	    let deadline = Instant::now() + snapback4_core::engine::command::ADMISSION_TIMEOUT;
   476	    let _advance = loop {
   477	        if Instant::now() >= deadline {
   478	            let why = super::committer::queue_error(snapback4_core::engine::command::SubmitError::Full).refusal();
   479	            return respond(request, 503, json!({"denied":why}));
   480	        }
   481	        match advance.try_lock() {
   482	            Ok(guard) => break guard,
   483	            Err(std::sync::TryLockError::Poisoned(error)) => break error.into_inner(),
   484	            Err(std::sync::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => std::thread::park_timeout(Duration::from_millis(1)),
   485	        }
   486	    };
   487	    let _advancing = Advancing(shared);
   488	    // @ref LLP 3000.009.001.000.000#9 — admitted clock work may outlive its acknowledgement; only the request owns the maintenance pause.
   489	    lock(&shared.maintenance).advancing = true;
   490	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — simulated time makes retries due without stealing a live worker's claim or viewer session.
   491	    let facts = super::RequestFacts::capture(&request);
   492	    // Retain publication facts independently of the worker's acknowledgement.
   493	    let published = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None));
   494	    let publication = published.clone();
   495	    let advanced = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
   496	        let before = crate::dev_clock_store::saved_boundaries(engine);
   497	        if let Some(principal) = &service {
   498	            if !shared.personas && engine.store().deployment_environment().map_err(|e|e.refusal())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(crate::dev_clock::release()); }
   499	            super::session_identity::mutation_authority(&facts,shared,engine,principal)?;
   500	        } else { shared.dev_authority(engine)?; }
   501	        let mut clock = lock(&shared.clock);
   502	        let floor = shared.time_audience_clock.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire);
   503	        let effective_before = clock.now().max(floor);
   504	        let mut next = clock.clone();
   505	        let now = (if milliseconds == 0 { next.now() } else { next.advance(milliseconds)? }).max(floor);
   506	        // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — refuse a saved boundary before any clock/session effect.
   507	        if drain && !allow_held && !shared.hold_schedules {
   508	            crate::dev_clock_store::refuse_held(engine, &before, clock.now(), now)?;
   509	        }
   510	        let boundaries = crate::dev_clock_store::crossed_boundaries(engine, &before, now, shared.hold_schedules || !drain, each_boundary)?;
   511	        if !shared.personas {
   512	            // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — a retained disclosure floor is also the credential authority clock.
   513	            // A raw jump below that floor advances no business time and cannot
   514	            // extend credentials or leases. Selection must never see an older
   515	            // raw process time and revive an already expired family.
   516	            let effective_delta = now.checked_sub(effective_before)
   517	                .ok_or_else(|| crate::dev_clock::input("effective clock advance overflow"))?;
   518	            let checkpoint = snapback4_core::metadata::StagingClock { now, offset: next.offset(), paused: true };
   519	            checkpoint_clock(engine, effective_delta, effective_before, preserve_sessions, &checkpoint).map_err(|e|e.refusal())?;
   520	        } else if service.is_some() {
   521	            let effective_delta = now.checked_sub(effective_before)
   522	                .ok_or_else(|| crate::dev_clock::input("effective clock advance overflow"))?;
   523	            engine.advance_staging_clock_at(effective_delta, effective_before, preserve_sessions).map_err(|e|e.refusal())?;
   524	        } else if milliseconds > 0 {
   525	            engine.advance_worker_leases_at(milliseconds, clock.now()).map_err(|e|e.refusal())?;
   526	        }
   527	        lock(&shared.maintenance).paused = true;
   528	        *clock = next;
   529	        *lock(&publication) = Some(now);
   530	        let offset = clock.offset();
   531	        let skew = now - snapback4_core::now_ms();
   532	        let isolated = if crate::dev_clock_store::has_data(engine) {
   533	            format!("; use {} for isolated time tests; clock advance --port N targets its printed port (guide jobs)", crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())
   534	        } else { String::new() };
   535	        let lifetime = if shared.personas { "development offset lasts until restart" } else { "offset persists with this staging store across restarts" };
   536	        let message = format!("cumulative offset {offset:+}ms (now includes the authoritative floor); {lifetime}{isolated}");
   537	        Ok((now, clock.now(), offset, skew, message, before, boundaries))
   538	    });
   539	    // Test the lost-ack branch after the real queued body publishes time.
