   613	/// `POST /dev/jobs/<job>` with `{"args":{..}}`: queue one run of a job as the
   614	/// system on the dev clock and drive chunks until it is done or parked. This is
   615	/// what `snapback4 run <job>` forwards to while dev owns the store.
   616	pub(super) fn run_job(request: Request, shared: &Shared, name: &str, body: &str) {
   617	    use snapback4_core::{JobState, error::Refusal, ir::ProgramKind, wire};
   618	    let service_route=request.url().starts_with("/jobs/");
   619	    let service=if service_route {
   620	        match super::session_identity::principal_of(&request,shared) {
   621	            Ok((principal,kind,snapback4_core::identity::SessionScope::Full)) if kind=="service" && principal.starts_with("service:") => Some(principal),
   622	            _ => return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_AUTH","auth","triggering a deployed system job requires a full service token").guide("jobs"))})),
   623	        }
   624	    } else {
   625	        if !shared.personas {return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&Refusal::new("E_AUTH","auth","/dev/jobs is a development door; use run <job> --release <dir> with a service token").guide("jobs"))}));}
   626	        None
   627	    };
   628	    let refuse = |request, status, refusal: Refusal| respond(request, status, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&refusal.guide("jobs"))}));
   629	    let payload: serde_json::Value = match serde_json::from_str(if body.trim().is_empty() { "{}" } else { body }) {
   630	        Ok(payload) => payload,
   631	        Err(error) => return refuse(request, 400, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("the request body is not JSON: {error}; send {{\"args\":{{..}}}}"))),
   632	    };
   633	    if service_route && !shared.personas {crate::release_requests::Scope::admit(&shared.release_requests,||*lock(&shared.generation));}
   634	    let program = lock(&shared.bound).programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == name).map(|p| p.program.clone());
   635	    let program = match program {
   636	        Some(program) if program.kind == ProgramKind::Job => program,
   637	        Some(other) => return refuse(request, 404, Refusal::new("E_OP", "op", format!("{name} is a {}, not a job; queries are POST /q/<op>, mutations POST /m/<op>", other.kind.word()))),
   638	        None => return respond(request, 404, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&super::dev_doors::stale(shared, Refusal::new("E_OP", "op", format!("unknown job {name}")).guide("jobs")))})),
   639	    };
   640	    if let Some(raw)=payload.get("args") && let Some(why)=super::dev_doors::persona_argument(shared,&program.args,raw) {return refuse(request,400,why);}
   641	    let mut args = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
   642	    if let Some(fields) = payload.get("args").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_object) {
   643	        for (field, value) in fields {
   644	            let Some(kind) = program.args.get(field) else { return refuse(request, 400, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("{name} takes no argument {field}"))); };
   645	            match wire::from_json(kind, value) {
   646	                Ok(typed) => { args.insert(field.clone(), typed); }
   647	                Err(why) => return refuse(request, 400, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("argument {field}: {why}"))),
   648	            }
   649	        }
   650	    }
   651	    let (facts, name) = (super::RequestFacts::capture(&request), name.to_owned());
   652	    let checked = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, shared| {
   653	        if !service_route { shared.dev_authority(engine)?; }
   654	        if let Some(service) = &service { super::session_identity::mutation_authority(&facts, shared, engine, service)?; }
   655	        Ok::<_, Refusal>(engine.enqueue_job(&name, args, shared.now()))
   656	    });
   657	    let queued = match checked { Ok(value) => value, Err(why) => return refuse(request, refusal_status(&why, 403), why) };
   658	    crate::release_requests::executed();
   659	    let id = match queued {
   660	        Ok(id) => id,
   661	        Err(error) => return respond(request, refusal_status(&error.refusal(), 400), json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   662	    };
   663	    // FIFO: earlier queued runs finish first, as with `run` on a stopped store;
   664	    // the background tick may run some chunks too, through the same engine.
   665	    let run = loop {
   666	        let job_id = id.clone();
   667	        let current = shared.engine.attempt(move |engine, _| engine.job(&job_id));
   668	        match current {
   669	            Ok(Some(run)) if matches!(run.state, JobState::Done | JobState::Parked) || crate::lifecycle::stopping() => break run,
   670	            Ok(Some(_)) => {}
   671	            Ok(None) => return respond(request, 500, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&RuntimeError::Store(format!("job {id} vanished")).refusal())})),
   672	            Err(error) => return respond(request, refusal_status(&error.refusal(), 500), json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   673	        }
   674	        let (chunk, logs) = engine_work(shared, move |engine, budget, shared| (engine.run_job_chunk_for(shared.now(), budget), engine.take_native_logs()));
   675	        for line in logs { snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: native {line}"); }
   676	        match chunk {
   677	            Ok(Some(chunk)) if chunk.state == JobState::Parked && shared.personas => shared.refusals.job(&chunk),
   678	            Ok(_) => {}
   679	            Err(error) => return respond(request, refusal_status(&error.refusal(), 500), json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   680	        }
   681	    };
   682	    snapback4_core::diagnostic!("snapback4: job {} {} on request: {} chunk{}, {} row{} written", run.name, if run.state == JobState::Done { "done" } else { "parked" },
   683	        run.chunks, if run.chunks == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, run.rows_written, if run.rows_written == 1 { "" } else { "s" });
   684	    respond(request, 200, json!({ "job": run.name, "id": run.id, "state": run.state, "chunks": run.chunks, "chunkSize": run.chunk_size, "retries": run.retries, "heapPeak": run.heap_peak, "rowsWritten": run.rows_written, "error": run.error }));
   685	}

   687	pub(super) fn clock_status(request: Request, shared: &Shared) {
   688	    if let Err(why) = clock_service(&request, shared) { return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&why)})); }
   689	    let result = (|| {
   690	        let (epoch, reader) = shared.reader()?;
   691	        let note = crate::dev_clock_store::ahead(&reader, shared.now());
   692	        lock(&shared.readers).put(&epoch, reader.into_inner());
   693	        note
   694	    })();
   695	    match result {
   696	        Ok(note) => { let now = shared.now(); respond(request, 200, json!({"storeAhead":note,"now":now,"skewMs":now - snapback4_core::now_ms()})) },
   697	        Err(error) => respond(request, refusal_status(&error.refusal(), 500), json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   698	    }
   699	}

const children = new Set<ChildProcess>();
const privateGroups = new WeakMap<ChildProcess, number>();
const groupClosures = new WeakMap<ChildProcess, Promise<void>>();
process.once("exit", () => { for (const child of children) child.kill("SIGKILL"); });
export function register(child: ChildProcess): void {
  children.add(child);
  child.once("exit", () => children.delete(child));
  child.on("error", () => children.delete(child));

export function deadline(ms: number | undefined, fallback: number): number {
  const value = ms ?? fallback;
  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 1) throw new RangeError("proof timeout must be positive and finite");
  return value;
}
/** @throws deadline expires; work rejection propagates. */
export async function bounded<T>(work: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  try {
    return await Promise.race([work, new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
      timer = setTimeout(() => reject(Error(`${label} timed out after ${ms} ms`)), ms);
    })]);
  } finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
}
/** Attempts every cleanup, even if a preceding step fails or stalls. */
/** @throws AggregateError after every cleanup was attempted; each step has a 10-second bound. */
export async function cleanup(...steps: Array<(() => unknown | Promise<unknown>) | undefined>): Promise<void> {
  const errors: unknown[] = [];
  for (const step of steps) if (step) {
    try { await bounded(Promise.resolve().then(step), 10_000, "proof cleanup"); }
    catch (error) { errors.push(error); }
  }
  if (errors.length) throw new AggregateError(errors, "proof cleanup failed");
}
/** @throws invalid handle/deadline, host stop failure or TERM/KILL reap deadline. */
export async function stopChild(child: ChildProcess | Pick<ProofHost, "url" | "stop">, graceMs = 5000): Promise<void> {
  deadline(graceMs, 5000);
  if (child && "url" in child && typeof child.url === "string" && typeof child.stop === "function") {
    await bounded(Promise.resolve().then(() => child.stop()), graceMs + 10_000, "host stop"); return;
  }
  if (!child || !("kill" in child) || typeof child.kill !== "function" || typeof child.once !== "function"
      || !(child.exitCode === null || typeof child.exitCode === "number")
      || !(child.signalCode === null || typeof child.signalCode === "string")) {
    throw new TypeError("stopChild needs a ChildProcess or { url, stop }");
  }
  if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) { await groupGone(child); return; }
  let done!: () => void;
  const exited = new Promise<void>(resolve => { done = resolve; });
  child.once("exit", done);
  child.once("error", done);
  try {
    child.kill("SIGTERM");
    try { await bounded(exited, graceMs, "SIGTERM"); }
    catch {
      child.kill("SIGKILL");
      await bounded(exited, 5000, "SIGKILL reap");
    }
  } finally { child.removeListener("exit", done); child.removeListener("error", done); }
  await groupGone(child);
}
async function groupGone(child: ChildProcess): Promise<void> {
  const pid = privateGroups.get(child);
  if (!pid || process.platform === "win32") return;
  const existing = groupClosures.get(child);
  if (existing) return existing;
  const cleanup = (async () => {
    const expires = performance.now() + 5000;
    for (;;) {
      try { process.kill(-pid, 0); }
      catch (error) { if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ESRCH") return; throw error; }
      const remaining = expires - performance.now();
      if (remaining <= 0) throw Error("proof process-group cleanup timed out after 5000 ms");
      await sleep(Math.min(10, remaining));
    }
  })();
  groupClosures.set(child, cleanup);
  return cleanup;
}
/** @throws partial, invalid or reversed PORT_LO/PORT_HI pair. */
export function portRange(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): string {
  const low = env.PORT_LO, high = env.PORT_HI;
  if (low === undefined && high === undefined) return "0";
  if (!low || !high || !/^\d+$/.test(low) || !/^\d+$/.test(high)
      || Number(low) < 1 || Number(high) > 65535 || Number(low) > Number(high)) {
    throw Error("PORT_LO and PORT_HI must both specify an inclusive range, 1 <= low <= high <= 65535");
  }
  return `${Number(low)}-${Number(high)}`;
}

export function logged(command: string, args: readonly string[], options: ProofOptions = {}) {
  const cwd = resolve(options.cwd ?? "."), id = randomUUID();
  const directory = logsDir(options); mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  const logs = { stdout: join(directory, `${id}.stdout.log`), stderr: join(directory, `${id}.stderr.log`) };
  if (options.secret) writeFileSync(logs.stdout, "stdout withheld: secret command (returned only to caller)\n", { flag: "wx", mode: 0o600 });
  const out = options.secret ? undefined : openSync(logs.stdout, "wx", 0o600), err = openSync(logs.stderr, "wx", 0o600);
  const grouped = options.processGroup === true && process.platform !== "win32";
  const executable = grouped ? process.execPath : command;
  const executableArgs = grouped ? [resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL("./proof-command.js", import.meta.url))), command, ...args] : [...args];
  let child: ChildProcess;
  try { child = spawn(executable, executableArgs, { cwd, detached: grouped || (options.detached ?? false), env: { ...(options.env ?? process.env), SNAPBACK4_PROOF_LAUNCH: id }, stdio: [grouped || options.livenessPipe ? "pipe" : "ignore", options.secret ? "pipe" : out!, err, ...(grouped ? ["ipc" as const] : [])] }); }
  finally { if (out !== undefined) closeSync(out); closeSync(err); }
  if (grouped && child.pid) privateGroups.set(child, child.pid);
  // Secret stdout never reaches a file, even briefly. Callers still receive it.
  let stdout = "";
  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
  child.stdout?.on("data", chunk => { stdout += chunk; });
  register(child);
  child.stdin?.on("error", () => {});
  let error: Error | undefined;
  let actualPid = child.pid;
  let actualCode: number | null = null;
  let actualSignal: NodeJS.Signals | null = null;
  let startedResolve!: () => void, startedReject!: (error: Error) => void, startedSettled = false;
  const started = new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => { startedResolve = resolve; startedReject = reject; });
  void started.catch(() => {}); // command() observes close/error instead; host startup awaits this promise.
  const didStart = () => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedResolve(); } };
  const failedStart = (value: unknown) => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedReject(value instanceof Error ? value : Error(String(value))); } };
  if (!grouped) didStart();
  child.on("message", message => {
    const event = message as {type?:string;pid?:number;code?:number|null;signal?:NodeJS.Signals|null;error?:string};
    if (event.type === "started" && typeof event.pid === "number") { actualPid = event.pid; didStart(); }
    if (event.type === "result") { actualCode = event.code ?? null; actualSignal = event.signal ?? null; if (event.error) error = Error(event.error); }
  });
  child.on("error", value => { error = value; failedStart(value); });
  const closed = new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => child.once("close", () => {
    failedStart(error ?? Error("proof command exited before its process-group handshake"));
    groupGone(child).then(resolve,reject);
  }));
  return { child, logs, id, closed, started, pid: () => actualPid, code: () => grouped ? actualCode : child.exitCode, signal: () => grouped ? actualSignal : child.signalCode, stdout: () => options.secret ? stdout : logText(logs.stdout), error: () => error };
}
export const logText = (path: string): string => readFileSync(path, "utf8");
export async function ready(run: ReturnType<typeof logged>, parse: (line: string) => string | undefined, timeoutMs: number): Promise<string> {
  const end = performance.now() + timeoutMs;
  let outAt = 0, errAt = 0;
  while (performance.now() < end) {
    if (run.error()) throw run.error();
    if (run.child.exitCode !== null || run.child.signalCode !== null) {
      throw Error(`proof child exited before ready (${run.child.exitCode ?? run.child.signalCode}); ${run.logs.stderr}\n${logText(run.logs.stderr).slice(-4000)}`);
    }
    for (const [path, offset, stream] of [[run.logs.stdout, outAt, "out"], [run.logs.stderr, errAt, "err"]] as const) {
      const text = logText(path);
      const complete = text.lastIndexOf("\n") + 1;
      for (const line of text.slice(offset, complete).split("\n")) {
        const url = parse(stripVTControlCharacters(line).trim());
        if (url) return url;
      }
      if (stream === "out") outAt = complete; else errAt = complete;
    }
    await sleep(25);
  }
  throw Error(`proof child ready timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms; logs: ${run.logs.stdout}, ${run.logs.stderr}`);
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#2-real-staging-accounts — real credentials and ordinary operator mutations, never system seeding or auth bypass.
/** @throws E_STAGING_INPUT for invalid plans; E_STAGING for production/dev hosts; E_STAGING_TIMEOUT, E_STAGING_SIGNUP or E_STAGING_PROVISION for incomplete setup. Partial accounts/grants may exist; inspect or discard the staging store before retrying. */
async function accounts(host: Pick<ServeHost, "url" | "operatorToken">, options: SeedAccountsOptions, environment: "staging" | "production"): Promise<StagingSessions> {
  // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — custom argument keys override defaults; the seat grants no extra authority.
  const service = options.service ?? "operator";
  const roles = Object.entries(options.roles), timeout = options.timeoutMs ?? 300_000;
  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(timeout) || timeout < 1 || !roles.length || roles.some(([role, n]) => !/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/.test(role) || !Number.isSafeInteger(n) || n < 1)
      || roles.reduce((sum, [, n]) => sum + n, 0) > 100 || !/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*$/.test(options.provision?.name ?? "")) {
    throw Error("E_STAGING_INPUT: provide 1..100 accounts across named roles, a mutation handle and a positive timeoutMs");
  }
  const end = performance.now() + timeout;
  const partial = environment === "staging" ? "inspect or discard this staging deployment" : "inspect partial production accounts/grants before retrying";
  const remaining = () => {
    const ms = Math.ceil(end - performance.now());
    if (ms <= 0) throw Error(`E_STAGING_TIMEOUT: setup incomplete; partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
    return ms;
  };
  const request = (path: string, init?: RequestInit) => fetch(host.url + path, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(Math.min(remaining(), 30_000)) });
  const config = await request("/auth/config");
  const identity = await config.json();
  if (!config.ok || identity.environment !== environment || identity.development !== false || !identity.password) {
    throw Error(environment === "staging"
      ? "E_STAGING: account seeding requires serve on a fresh deploy --staging with password identity; production and dev refuse before creating users"
      : "E_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNTS: account provisioning requires serve on a production deploy with password identity; staging and dev refuse before creating users");
  }
  const operator = await host.operatorToken(service);
  if (environment === "production") {
    const response = await request("/schema", { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${operator}` } }), schema = await response.json();
    const named = response.ok && Array.isArray(schema.service_identities) && schema.service_identities.includes(`service:${service}`);
    if (!named) process.stderr.write(`snapback4: WARNING minted service:${service}, but the served schema reports no explicit positive authorization mention for that service identity; rules still decide every operation and provisionAccounts(${options.provision.name}) will likely refuse.\n`);
  }
  const sessions: StagingSessions = Object.create(null);
  for (const [role, count] of roles) {
    sessions[role] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const email = `${environment}-${role}-${randomUUID()}@example.test`, password = randomBytes(24).toString("base64url");
      const {json: reply} = await identityRequest(host.url + "/auth/signup", {
        method:"POST", headers:{"content-type":"application/json"}, body:JSON.stringify({email,password}),
      }, fetch, {timeoutMs:remaining()}).catch(error => {
        if ((error as {code?: string})?.code === "E_IDENTITY_TIMEOUT") throw Error(`E_STAGING_TIMEOUT: signup deadline expired; partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
        remaining(); throw error;
      });
      if ((reply.denied as {code?:string} | undefined)?.code === "E_RATE_LIMIT") {
        throw Error("E_STAGING_TIMEOUT: identity retry budget exhausted; increase timeoutMs or inspect partial accounts/grants before retrying");
      }
      const session = reply.session as {principal?:string;kind?:string;token?:string;expiresAt?:number} | undefined;
      if (typeof session?.principal !== "string" || typeof session.token !== "string" || typeof session.expiresAt !== "number" || session.kind !== "user") {
        throw Error(`E_STAGING_SIGNUP: signup refused (${(reply.denied as {code?:string} | undefined)?.code ?? "invalid reply"}); partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
      }
      const account: StagingAccount = { kind: session.kind, role, email, password, principal: session.principal, token: session.token, expiresAt: session.expiresAt };
      const args = { principal: account.principal, role, ...options.args?.(account) };
      const response = await request(`/m/${options.provision.name}`, { method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json", authorization: `Bearer ${operator}` }, body: JSON.stringify({ id: randomUUID(), args }) });
      const result = await response.json();
      if (!response.ok || result.state !== "sent") throw Error(`E_STAGING_PROVISION: ${options.provision.name} refused (${result.why?.code ?? result.denied?.code ?? "invalid reply"}); partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
      sessions[role]!.push(account);
    }
  }
  return sessions;
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#2-real-staging-accounts — real credentials and ordinary operator mutations, never system seeding or auth bypass.
/** @throws E_STAGING_INPUT for invalid plans; E_STAGING for production/dev hosts; E_STAGING_TIMEOUT, E_STAGING_SIGNUP or E_STAGING_PROVISION for incomplete setup. */
export function seedAccounts(host: Pick<ServeHost, "url" | "operatorToken">, options: SeedAccountsOptions): Promise<StagingSessions> {
  return accounts(host, options, "staging");
}

/** Create real production password accounts and provision each one through the
 * same ordinary service-authorized mutation contract as seedAccounts.
 * @throws E_STAGING_INPUT for invalid plans; E_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNTS for staging/dev;

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — production setup shares the plan without acquiring fixture authority.
export function provisionAccounts(host: Pick<ServeHost, "url" | "operatorToken">, options: SeedAccountsOptions): Promise<ProvisionedSessions> {
  return accounts(host, options, "production");

   127	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#2-real-staging-accounts — operator authority stays in the existing local store proof; bulk setup refuses production.
   128	/** Starts a release. stop() awaits native exit and kernel store release.
   129	 * @throws E_PROOF_USAGE for missing deployment directory; child exit, readiness deadline or served identity mismatch. stop() rejects bounded cleanup failure. */
   130	export async function startServe(deployDir: string, options: ServeOptions | readonly string[] = {}): Promise<ServeHost> {
   131	  if (typeof deployDir !== "string" || !deployDir.trim()) throw Object.assign(new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: startServe(deployDir, options) requires a deployment directory as its first argument"), { code: "E_PROOF_USAGE" });
   132	  const opts: ServeOptions = Array.isArray(options) ? { args: options } : options as ServeOptions;
   133	  const directory = resolve(opts.cwd ?? ".", deployDir);
   134	  if (opts.clockOffset !== undefined && (typeof opts.clockOffset !== "string" || !/^[+-]?\d+(ms|s|m|h|d|w)$/.test(opts.clockOffset))) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: clockOffset is a signed duration such as +25h");
   135	  if (opts.clockOffset !== undefined && opts.args?.some(arg => arg === "--clock-offset" || arg.startsWith("--clock-offset="))) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: pass clockOffset once");
   136	  const host = await nativeHost("serve", [directory], { ...opts, args: [...(opts.args ?? []), ...(opts.clockOffset === undefined ? [] : ["--clock-offset", opts.clockOffset])] });
   137	  const clockCall = async (body?: object): Promise<ClockAdvance> => {
   138	    const config = await fetchIdentity(`${host.url}/auth/config`, deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 10_000));
   139	    if (!config.response.ok || config.body.environment !== "staging") throw Error("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY: clock controls require a deploy --staging store");
   140	    const clockToken = served.operatorToken("clock");
   141	    const response = await fetch(`${host.url}/dev/clock/${body ? "advance" : "status"}`, { method: body ? "POST" : "GET", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${await clockToken}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, ...(body ? { body: JSON.stringify(body) } : {}), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 60_000)) });
   142	    const result = await response.json() as Partial<ClockAdvance> & { sessionNotice?: string; denied?: { code?: string; message?: string } };
   143	    if (result.sessionNotice) process.stderr.write(`snapback4: ${result.sessionNotice}\n`);
   144	    if (!response.ok || result.denied || !Number.isSafeInteger(result.now)) throw Object.assign(Error(`staging clock refused or reply unavailable; inspect clock and queued work before retrying: ${result.denied?.code ?? response.status} ${result.denied?.message ?? ""}`), { report: result });
   145	    if (body && (!Array.isArray(result.fired) || !Array.isArray(result.held))) throw Error("staging clock reply has no schedule report; inspect clock and queued work before retrying");
   146	    for (const schedule of result.held ?? []) if (schedule.holdCode === "saved-boundary") process.stderr.write(`snapback4: schedule ${schedule.name}: ${schedule.reason}\n`);
   147	    const report: ClockAdvance = { now: result.now!, fired: result.fired ?? [], held: result.held ?? [], maintenancePaused: result.maintenancePaused ?? false, valueOf() { return this.now; } };
   148	    return report;
   149	  };
   150	  // Exit can precede inherited watchdog flock release. The private local
   151	  // barrier observes the same canonical ownership sidecar without writing data.
   152	  let stopping: Promise<void> | undefined;
   153	  const stop = () => stopping ??= (async () => {
   154	    await host.stop();
   155	    const result = await cli(["serve", directory, "--wait-stopped"], {...opts, timeoutMs:6000});
   156	    if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof serve store release failed: ${result.stderr}`);
   157	  })().catch(error => { stopping = undefined; throw error; });
   158	  const served: ServeHost = { ...host, stop,
   159	    now: async () => (await clockCall()).now,
   160	    advance: (duration, options = {}) => {
   161	      if (typeof duration !== "string" || (!/^\+?\d+(ms|s|m|h|d|w)$/.test(duration) || BigInt(duration.replace(/\D/g, "")) === 0n)) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: advance requires a positive whole duration");
   162	      return clockCall({ duration, ...options });
   163	    },
   164	    drain: (options = {}) => clockCall({ duration: "0ms", drain: true, ...options }),
   165	    operatorToken: async (service = "operator", days = 1) => {
   166	      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(days) || days < 1 || days > 3650) throw Error("proof operatorToken: invalid service or days (1..3650)");
   167	      const result = await cli(["token", "--service", service, "--days", String(days), "--release", directory, "--quiet"], opts);
   168	      if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof operator token refused: ${result.stderr}`);
   169	      const token = result.stdout.trim();
   170	      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(token)) throw Error("proof operator token malformed");
   171	      return token;
   172	    },
   173	    seedAccounts: accountOptions => seedAccounts(served, accountOptions),
   174	    provisionAccounts: accountOptions => provisionAccounts(served, accountOptions),
   175	  };
   176	  try {
   177	    if (opts.seedUsers && opts.provisionUsers) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: choose seedUsers for staging or provisionUsers for production");
   178	    if (opts.seedUsers) served.sessions = await served.seedAccounts(opts.seedUsers);
   179	    if (opts.provisionUsers) served.sessions = await served.provisionAccounts(opts.provisionUsers);
   180	    return served;
   181	  }
   182	  catch (error) { await served.stop(); throw error; }
   183	}
   184	async function frontend(kind: "static" | "vite", dir: string, options: ProofOptions): Promise<ProofHost> {
   185	  const env = { ...process.env, ...options.env }, ports = portRange(env), timeout = deadline(options.timeoutMs, 30_000);
   186	  const cwd = resolve(options.cwd ?? ".");
   187	  const directory = resolve(cwd, dir);
   188	  // Vite is resolved from the app, never the proof package's development dependencies.
   189	  const vite = kind === "vite" ? createRequire(resolve(directory, "package.json")).resolve("vite") : "";
   190	  const run = logged(process.execPath, [fileURLToPath(new URL("./proof-host.js", import.meta.url)), kind, directory, ports, vite], { ...options, env, detached: process.platform !== "win32", livenessPipe: true });
   191	  try {
   192	    const url = await ready(run, line => {
   193	      const match = line.match(/^SNAPBACK4_PROOF_READY (\{.*\})$/);
   194	      if (!match) return;
   195	      const data = JSON.parse(match[1]!);
   196	      if (data.pid !== run.child.pid || data.kind !== kind) throw Error("proof frontend PID mismatch");
   197	      return data.url as string;
   198	    }, timeout);
   199	    const response = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeout) });
   200	    if (response.headers.get("x-snapback4-proof") !== String(run.child.pid) + ":" + run.id) throw Error("proof frontend identity mismatch");
   201	    await response.body?.cancel();
   202	    return { url, pid: run.child.pid!, logs: run.logs, stop: () => stopChild(run.child, deadline(options.stopTimeoutMs, 5000)) };
   203	  } catch (error) { await stopChild(run.child, deadline(options.stopTimeoutMs, 5000)); throw error; }
   204	}

   210	export interface CliResult { code: number | null; signal: NodeJS.Signals | null; stdout: string; stderr: string; logs: ProofHost["logs"] }
   211	/** Waits for close (stdio drained), never merges the two streams. Nonzero is returned for refusal assertions. */
   212	/** @throws spawn error or command deadline; nonzero exit is returned in code, not thrown. */
   213	export function cli(args: readonly string[], options: ProofOptions = {}): Promise<CliResult> {
   214	  return command(process.execPath, [fileURLToPath(new URL("../bin/snapback4.js", import.meta.url)), ...args], { ...options, secret: options.secret || args[0] === "token" });
   215	}
   216	/** A bounded directly spawned build/tool command, with the same file logs. */
   217	/** @throws spawn error or command deadline; nonzero exit is returned in code, not thrown. */
   218	export async function command(binary: string, args: readonly string[], options: ProofOptions = {}): Promise<CliResult> {
   219	  const run = logged(binary, args, { ...options, processGroup: true, env: { ...process.env, ...options.env } });
   220	  try {
   221	    await bounded(run.closed, deadline(options.timeoutMs, 120_000), "proof cli close");
   222	    if (run.error()) throw run.error();
   223	    return { code: run.code(), signal: run.signal(), stdout: run.stdout(), stderr: logText(run.logs.stderr), logs: run.logs };
   224	  } catch (error) { await stopChild(run.child, deadline(options.stopTimeoutMs, 5000)); throw error; }
   225	  finally { run.child.stdout?.destroy(); } // Secret capture must not pin the driver after a deadline.
   226	}
   227	async function successful(args: string[], options: ProofOptions) {
   228	  const result = await cli(args, options);
   229	  if (result.code !== 0) {
   230	    const stdout = result.stdout.trimEnd();
   231	    const tail = stdout.length > 4000 ? `…${stdout.slice(-4000)}` : stdout;
   232	    throw Error(`proof CLI failed (${result.code}): ${result.stderr}; stdout tail: ${tail || "(empty)"}; logs: ${result.logs.stderr}`);
   233	  }
   234	  return result;
   235	}

   246	// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000.000#11-wave-14-truthful-starter-custody-day4 — saved-source proof results expose authored cases separately from query sweeps.
   247	export interface TestSourceOptions extends ProofOptions { fixtureOnly?: boolean }
   248	export interface TestSourceResult extends CliResult { casesRun: number; casesSkipped: number }
   249	/** @throws missing source, CLI failure, invalid business-case summary or zero cases without fixtureOnly. */
   250	export function testSource(source: string, options: TestSourceOptions = {}): Promise<TestSourceResult> {
   251	  if (typeof source !== "string" || !source) throw Error(`proof testSource requires an explicit saved source file or directory; got ${JSON.stringify(source) ?? String(source)}: pass versions/v1`);
   252	  const { fixtureOnly = false, ...proofOptions } = options;
   253	  return successful(["test", "--source", source, ...(fixtureOnly ? ["--fixture-only"] : []), ...(proofOptions.args ?? [])], proofOptions).then(result => {
   254	    const summaries = [...result.stdout.matchAll(/^SNAPBACK4_TEST_CASES (\{.*\})$/gm)];
   255	    if (summaries.length !== 1) throw Error(`proof testSource received no unique business-case summary; stdout tail: ${result.stdout.trimEnd().slice(-4000) || "(empty)"}; logs: ${result.logs.stdout}`);
   256	    let cases: { run: number; skipped: number };
   257	    try { cases = JSON.parse(summaries[0]![1]!) as { run: number; skipped: number }; }
   258	    catch { throw Error(`proof testSource received a malformed business-case summary: ${summaries[0]![0]}; logs: ${result.logs.stdout}`); }
   259	    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(cases.run) || cases.run < 0 || !Number.isSafeInteger(cases.skipped) || cases.skipped < 0) {
   260	      throw Error(`proof testSource received invalid business-case counts: ${summaries[0]![0]}; logs: ${result.logs.stdout}`);
   261	    }
   262	    if (cases.run === 0 && !fixtureOnly) {
   263	      throw Error(`proof testSource ran no business cases (${cases.skipped} skipped); add test.cases.jsonl for this saved version, or pass { fixtureOnly: true } when fixture loading alone is the intended proof; stdout tail: ${result.stdout.trimEnd().slice(-4000) || "(empty)"}`);
   264	    }
   265	    return { ...result, casesRun: cases.run, casesSkipped: cases.skipped };
   266	  });
   267	}

   270	export function sandboxUnavailable(error: unknown): boolean {
   271	  return /No usable sandbox|Running as root without --no-sandbox|Failed to move to new namespace|SUID sandbox|sandbox.*Operation not permitted|Failed to unshare.*Operation not permitted/i.test(String(error));

   273	/** @throws E_PROOF_BROWSER for missing playwright-core; invalid deadline, browser launch failure or callback error; bounded context/browser cleanup failure. */
   274	export async function withBrowser<T>(options: LaunchOptions & Pick<ProofOptions, "cwd" | "logsDir"> & { chromium?: BrowserType }, proof: (context: BrowserContext) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
   275	  const { chromium: suppliedChromium, executablePath, cwd: _cwd, logsDir: _logs, ...other } = options;
   276	  const requireCaller = createRequire(resolve(options.cwd ?? process.cwd(), "package.json"));
   277	  let caller = suppliedChromium;
   278	  {
   279	    for (const peer of ["playwright-core", "@playwright/test", "playwright"]) {
   280	      let path: string;
   281	      try { path = requireCaller.resolve(peer); }
   282	      catch (error) { if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "MODULE_NOT_FOUND") continue; throw error; }
   283	      const peerModule = await import(path);
   284	      await registerRenderedSelector(peerModule.selectors ?? peerModule.default?.selectors);
   285	      caller ??= (peerModule.chromium ?? peerModule.default?.chromium) as BrowserType;
   286	      break;
   287	    }
   288	  }
   289	  if (!caller) {
   290	    try { caller = (await import("playwright-core")).chromium; }
   291	    catch (cause) { throw new Error("E_PROOF_BROWSER: withBrowser requires playwright-core; run npm install --save-dev playwright-core before deploying or starting proof hosts", { cause }); }
   292	  }
   293	  const directory = logsDir(options); mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
   294	  const err = openSync(join(directory, `${randomUUID()}.browser.stderr.log`), "wx", 0o600);
   295	  const diagnostic = openSync(join(directory, `${randomUUID()}.witness.private.jsonl`), "wx", 0o600);
   296	
   297	  const launch = { ...other, ...(executablePath === undefined ? {} : { executablePath }), timeout: deadline(options.timeout, 30_000), logger: {
   298	    isEnabled: () => true,
   299	    log: (name: string, severity: string, message: string | Error) => { writeSync(err, `${name} ${severity}: ${String(message)}\n`); },
   300	  } };
   301	  const args = [...(options.args ?? [])];
   302	  if (process.getuid?.() === 0 && !args.includes("--no-sandbox")) args.push("--no-sandbox");
   303	  // Playwright owns its browser child over a pipe, including parent-exit cleanup.
   304	  // No WebSocket server or TCP debugging port is opened.
   305	  let browser;
   306	  try {
   307	    try { browser = await caller.launch({ ...launch, args, chromiumSandbox: !args.includes("--no-sandbox") }); }
   308	    catch (error) {
   309	      if (args.includes("--no-sandbox") || !sandboxUnavailable(error)) throw error;
   310	      browser = await caller.launch({ ...launch, args: [...args, "--no-sandbox"], chromiumSandbox: false });
   311	    }
   312	    let context: BrowserContext | undefined;
   313	    try {
   314	      context = await browser.newContext();
   315	      await context.exposeBinding("__snapback4ProofDiagnostic", (_source, value: unknown) => {
   316	        writeSync(diagnostic, `${JSON.stringify(value)}\n`);
   317	      });
   318	      // Init scripts run on each document, including HTTP redirect destinations,
   319	      // before any application script samples its URL.
   320	      await context.addInitScript(() => {
   321	        if (window.top !== window || !/^https?:$/.test(location.protocol)) return;
   322	        const url = new URL(location.href);
   323	        url.searchParams.set("witness", "web");
   324	        history.replaceState(history.state, "", url.href);
   325	      });
   326	      // The bridge function is self-contained after TypeScript erases types.
   327	      // Proof code lives in this realm, outside the application's bundle.
   328	      await context.addInitScript({ content: webWitnessObserverScript() });
   329	      context.setDefaultTimeout(30_000); context.setDefaultNavigationTimeout(30_000);
   330	      return await proof(context);
   331	    } finally {
   332	      try { if (context) await bounded(context.close(), 5000, "browser context close"); }
   333	      finally { await bounded(browser.close(), 5000, "browser close"); }
   334	    }
   335	  } finally { closeSync(err); closeSync(diagnostic); }
   336	}
   337	const substringLocators = new WeakMap<Locator, { locator: Locator; scoped: boolean }>();
   338	/** Match the smallest visible element whose composed descendant text matches.
   339	 * Strings normalize whitespace and stay exact by default; regexes keep their
   340	 * own semantics. Editable values never count. Independent matches remain
   341	 * ambiguous, including repeated rows. */
   342	/** @throws None at construction; locator observation can refuse ambiguous or invalid selectors. */
   343	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — composed text preserves exactness and ambiguity.
   344	export function renderedText(page: Page, text: string | RegExp, options: { within?: Locator; exact?: boolean } | null = {}): Locator {
   345	  const normalized = options ?? {};
   346	  const root = normalized.within ?? page;
   347	  const match = (exact: boolean) => registeredLocator(root.locator(`${renderedSelector}=${JSON.stringify({
   348	    source: typeof text === "string" ? text : text.source,
   349	    flags: typeof text === "string" ? "" : text.flags,
   350	    regex: typeof text !== "string", exact,
   351	  })}`));
   352	  const locator = match(normalized.exact ?? true);
   353	  if (typeof text === "string" && normalized.exact !== false) substringLocators.set(locator, { locator: match(false), scoped: normalized.within !== undefined });
   354	  return locator;
   355	}

   357	export interface ExhaustPagesOptions {
   358	  /** Refuse rather than loop forever when a backend returns bad continuations. */
   359	  maxPages?: number;
   360	  /** Names the read in a refusal without exposing its rows or cursor. */
   361	  label?: string;
   362	}
   363	type ProofPage<Row> =
   364	  | { readonly data: readonly Row[]; readonly next?: Cursor | null; readonly complete: boolean; readonly cut: ReadCut; readonly existence?: "present" | "absent" | "partial" }
   365	  | { readonly denied: Refusal }
   366	  | { readonly loading: true };
   367	/** Read every page by passing each opaque `next` back unchanged. The callback
   368	 * receives null first. Refusals, loading, malformed/repeated cursors and a
   369	 * capped or incomplete page fail instead of returning a partial snapshot. */
   370	/** @throws E_PROOF_PAGE for a refused, loading, malformed, repeated, incomplete or over-limit traversal; callback errors propagate. */
   371	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — proof traversal must never promote capped or partial reads to complete evidence.
   372	export async function exhaustPages<Row>(readPage: (cursor: Cursor | null) => Promise<ProofPage<Row>>, options: ExhaustPagesOptions = {}): Promise<Row[]> {
   373	  const maxPages = options.maxPages ?? 1_000, label = options.label ?? "paged read";
   374	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(maxPages) || maxPages < 1) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: maxPages must be a positive safe integer`);
   375	  const rows: Row[] = [], seen = new Set<string>();
   376	  let cursor: Cursor | null = null;
   377	  for (let pageNumber = 1; pageNumber <= maxPages; pageNumber++) {
   378	    const page = await readPage(cursor);
   379	    if (!page || typeof page !== "object") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned no read envelope`);
   380	    if ("denied" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} refused ${page.denied.code}: ${page.denied.message}`);
   381	    if ("loading" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is still loading`);
   382	    if (!Array.isArray(page.data)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} data is not an array`);
   383	    if (page.cut !== null) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (${page.cut === undefined ? "missing" : page.cut} cut)`);
   384	    if (page.complete !== true) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (complete must be true)`);
   385	    if (page.existence === "partial") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} has partial existence`);
   386	    rows.push(...page.data);
   387	    const next = page.next ?? null;
   388	    if (next === null) return rows;
   389	    if (typeof next !== "string" || next.length === 0) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a malformed cursor`);
   390	    if (seen.has(next)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a repeated cursor`);
   391	    seen.add(next);
   392	    cursor = next as Cursor;
   393	  }
   394	  throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: exceeded maxPages ${maxPages}`);
   395	}

   401	/** @throws observation deadline with scoped locator, last text and visible headings; selector ambiguity is propagated. */
   402	export async function waitForFresh(locator: Locator, previous: string | null, options: number | { within?: Locator; timeoutMs?: number } = 30_000): Promise<string> {
   403	  const timeoutMs = deadline(typeof options === "number" ? options : options.timeoutMs, 30_000);

   405	  locator = registeredLocator(locator);
   406	  if (typeof options !== "number" && options.within) {
   407	    locator = registeredLocator(options.within.locator(locator));
   408	    if (substring) substring = { locator: options.within.locator(substring.locator), scoped: true };
   409	  }
   410	  const end = performance.now() + timeoutMs;

    fn drop(&mut self) { if !self.complete && !self.refresh { let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.path); } }

    pub(super) fn prepare(project: &Project, sources: &[(String,String)], bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound, options: &Options, deployment: &std::path::Path) -> Result<Option<Self>,String> {
        let Some(name) = options.flags.get("save-version") else {return Ok(None);};
        if sources.is_empty() || sources.iter().all(|(_,text)|text.trim().is_empty()) {return Err("not saved yet: a saved version needs nonempty Quarry source".into());}
        if options.flags.contains_key("check") {return Err("--save-version captures a successful deployment; omit --check to save, or omit --save-version for a read-only preview".into());}
        if project.root.canonicalize().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.starts_with(deployment.canonicalize().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?) {
            return Err("cannot save a version inside deployment custody; run deploy from the application's source directory".into());
        }
        let suffix = name.strip_prefix("versions/v").ok_or("--save-version needs a new project-relative versions/vN directory")?;
        if suffix.is_empty() || suffix.starts_with('0') || !suffix.bytes().all(|b|b.is_ascii_digit()) {return Err("--save-version needs versions/vN with a positive numeric N".into());}
        let parent=project.root.join("versions");
        if std::fs::symlink_metadata(&parent).is_ok_and(|m|m.file_type().is_symlink()) {return Err("--save-version refuses a symlinked versions directory".into());}
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&parent).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
        let path=project.root.join(name);
        let refresh = match std::fs::symlink_metadata(&path) {
            Ok(meta) if meta.file_type().is_symlink() || !meta.is_dir() => return Err(format!("cannot refresh {name}: saved version must be a real directory")),
            Ok(_) => {
                let selected=sources.iter().cloned().collect::<BTreeMap<_,_>>();
                let existing=crate::client_compatibility::sources(&path).map_err(|e|format!("cannot refresh {name}: {e}"))?.into_iter().collect::<BTreeMap<_,_>>();
                if existing != selected {return Err(format!("cannot refresh {name}: selected source differs from the saved source; choose a new versions/vN"));}
                true
            }
            Err(error) if error.kind()==std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {std::fs::create_dir(&path).map_err(|e|format!("cannot save {name}: {e}"))?;false}
            Err(error) => return Err(format!("cannot inspect {name}: {error}")),
        };
        let mut files = if refresh {Vec::new()} else {sources.iter().map(|(name,text)|(PathBuf::from(name),text.as_bytes().to_vec())).collect()};
        files.push((PathBuf::from("generated/api.ts"),snapback4_lang::emit::typescript(bound).into_bytes()));
        files.push((PathBuf::from("generated/package.json"),crate::project::GENERATED_PACKAGE.as_bytes().to_vec()));
        let mut saved=Self {path,files,complete:false,refresh};
        let fixture = match options.flags.get("schema").map(PathBuf::from) {
            None=>project.root.join("fixtures"),
            Some(source) if source.is_dir()=>source.join("fixtures"),
            Some(source) if source.file_name().is_some_and(|n|n=="schema.q")=>source.parent().unwrap().join("fixtures"),
            Some(source)=>source.with_file_name(format!("{}-fixtures",source.file_stem().unwrap_or_default().to_string_lossy())),
        };
        if fixture.is_dir() && !refresh {
            let mut entries=std::fs::read_dir(&fixture).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            entries.sort_by_key(|e|e.file_name());
            for entry in entries {
                if entry.path().extension().is_some_and(|e|e=="jsonl") || entry.file_name()=="test.sweep.json" {
                    if !entry.file_type().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.is_file() {return Err("saved fixtures must be regular files".into());}
                    saved.files.push((PathBuf::from("fixtures").join(entry.file_name()),std::fs::read(entry.path()).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?));
                }
            }
        }
        if !refresh {saved.files.push((PathBuf::from("fixtures/.gitkeep"),Vec::new()));}
        Ok(Some(saved))
    }
    pub(super) fn finish(&mut self, release: u64, source_hash: &str) -> Result<(),String> {
        self.files.push((PathBuf::from("release.json"),format!("{}\n",serde_json::json!({"release":release,"sourceHash":source_hash,"cliVersion":env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")})).into_bytes()));
        for (name,bytes) in &self.files {
            let path=self.path.join(name);
            std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap()).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if self.refresh {
                let temporary=path.with_extension(format!("refresh-{}",std::process::id()));
                std::fs::write(&temporary,bytes).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
                std::fs::rename(&temporary,&path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            } else {
                use std::io::Write;
                let mut file=std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).open(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
                file.write_all(bytes).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            }
        }
        self.complete=true;
        eprintln!("{} release {release} sources, generated client, contemporary fixtures and release.json at {}",if self.refresh {"refreshed"} else {"saved"},self.path.display());
        Ok(())
    }
}

  204	                if let Some(tail) = statement[offset..].strip_prefix(flag) {
  205	                    if tail.is_empty() || tail.starts_with(char::is_whitespace) || tail.starts_with('=') { return Some(flag); }
  206	                }
  207	            }
  208	        }
  209	    }
  210	    None
  211	}

  217	    let Some(root) = path.parent().and_then(Path::parent) else { return String::new(); };
  218	    let mut dirs = Vec::new();
  219	    if root.join("store.sqlite").is_file() { dirs.push(root.to_path_buf()); }

    30	pub(crate) fn existing_deployment(requested: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    31	    let missing = || format!("no current release in {}; run `snapback4 deploy {}` first", requested.display(), requested.display());
    32	    if !requested.join("store.sqlite").is_file() { return Err(missing()); }

    38	// SQLite READONLY can create WAL sidecars. A stopped store's existing owner
    39	// lock makes immutable inspection safe; a live host supplies its own status.
    40	fn inspect_current(dir: &Path) -> Result<u64, String> {
    41	    let database = dir.join("store.sqlite").canonicalize().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    42	    let missing = || format!("no current release in {}; run `snapback4 deploy {}` first", dir.display(), dir.display());
    43	    let owner = match snapback4_core::private_fs::auxiliary_file(&database,
    44	        &snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_path(&database), false, 0) {
    45	        Ok(owner) => owner,
    46	        Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
    47	            // Relocated/legacy deployments may not yet have a sidecar beside
    48	            // the resolved DB. Establish a complete current source first; only
    49	            // a known deployment may let SQLite create its ordinary WAL files.
    50	            return pointer_current(dir, &database);
    51	        },
    52	        Err(error) => return Err(format!("{}; existing ownership sidecar unavailable: {error}", missing())),
    53	    };
    54	    match owner.try_lock() {
    55	        Ok(()) => {},
    56	        Err(std::fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => {
    57	            match crate::release_control::request(dir, crate::release_control::Command::Status {after:0, items_after:None, event:None}) {
    58	                Ok(status) => return status["release"].as_u64().filter(|n|*n>0).ok_or_else(missing),
    59	                Err(error) => {
    60	                    // A killed host's watchdogs retain ownership during their
    61	                    // bounded cleanup. Preserve serve's existing restart wait.
    62	                    if !crate::store_owner::stopped_host(&database) {
    63	                        // A second source directory may alias the same DB. Its
    64	                        // source cannot control this host, but its token still
    65	                        // belongs to the resolved database. Establish current
    66	                        // source before permitting ordinary read-only WAL work.
    67	                        return pointer_current(dir, &database).map_err(|_| format!("{}; {error}",missing()));
    68	                    }
    69	                    let deadline=std::time::Instant::now()+std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);
    70	                    loop {
    71	                        match owner.try_lock() {
    72	                            Ok(()) => break,
    73	                            Err(std::fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) if std::time::Instant::now()<deadline => std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(25)),
    74	                            _ => return Err(format!("{}; {error}",missing())),
    75	                        }
    76	                    }
    77	                }
    78	            }
    79	        },
    80	        Err(error) => return Err(error.to_string()),
    81	    }
    82	    if !snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_is_named(&database, &owner) {
    83	        return Err("store ownership changed during release inspection; retry".into());
    84	    }
    85	    #[cfg(unix)]
    86	    let bytes = { use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt; database.as_os_str().as_bytes() };
    87	    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    88	    let bytes = database.to_str().ok_or("invalid store path")?.as_bytes();
    89	    let mut uri = String::from("file:");
    90	    for byte in bytes {
    91	        if byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"/._-".contains(byte) { uri.push(*byte as char); }
    92	        else { uri.push_str(&format!("%{byte:02X}")); }
    93	    }
    94	    let mut wal = database.as_os_str().to_os_string(); wal.push("-wal"); let wal = PathBuf::from(wal);
    95	    let mut shm = database.as_os_str().to_os_string(); shm.push("-shm"); let shm = PathBuf::from(shm);
    96	    let has_wal = match std::fs::metadata(&wal) {
    97	        Ok(meta) => meta.len() > 0,
    98	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => false,
    99	        Err(e) => return Err(e.to_string()),
   100	    };
   101	    if has_wal && !shm.is_file() { return Err("store has a WAL without its shared-memory sidecar; run deploy on this stopped deployment to recover it before inspection".into()); }
   102	    // Immutable SQLite omits WAL reads: use it only for the checkpointed main
   103	    // image. Existing WAL+SHM can be read normally under the same exclusion.
   104	    uri.push_str(if has_wal { "?mode=ro" } else { "?mode=ro&immutable=1" });
   105	    let inspection = snapback4_core::store_port::AnyInspection::open_uri(&uri).map_err(|(_, e)|e)?;
   106	    let release = inspection.optional_release().map_err(|(_, e)|e)?;
   107	    let release = match release {
   108	        Some(value) => value,
   109	        None => std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("current")).map_err(|_| missing())?,
   110	    };
   111	    release.trim().parse::<u64>().ok().filter(|n|*n>0).ok_or_else(missing)
   112	}

   120	    let missing = || format!("no current release in {}; deploy first", dir.display());

   136	fn current(dir: &Path, owner: &Owner) -> Result<Option<u64>, String> {
   137	    let database = dir.join("store.sqlite");
   138	    if database.exists() {
   139	        let store = owner
   140	            .open_store(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
   141	            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   142	        if let Some(release) = store.release_value().map_err(|e| e.to_string())? {
   143	            return release
   144	                .parse()
   145	                .map(Some)
   146	                .map_err(|_| "invalid release identity in store".into());
   147	        }
   148	    }
   149	    // Compatibility with deployments made before the database owned this
   150	    // pointer. The next activation records it transactionally.
   151	    match std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("current")) {
   152	        Ok(text) => text
   153	            .trim()
   154	            .parse()
   155	            .map(Some)
   156	            .map_err(|_| "invalid current release file".into()),
   157	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
   158	        Err(e) => Err(format!("cannot read current release: {e}")),
   159	    }
   160	}
   161	pub(super) fn bound_at(root: PathBuf) -> Result<snapback4_lang::Bound, String> {
   162	    let project = Project { root };
   163	    if project.sources().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.is_empty() {
   164	        return Err("release has no Quarry source; select a complete immutable release".into());
   165	    }
   166	    let bound = project.compile().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   167	    if !bound.diagnostics.is_empty() {
   168	        return Err(bound
   169	            .diagnostics
   170	            .iter()
   171	            .map(ToString::to_string)
   172	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
   173	            .join("\n"));
   174	    }
   175	    Ok(bound)
   176	}
   177	fn check_change(
   178	    dir: &Path,
   179	    previous: Option<u64>,
   180	    bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound,
   181	    options: &Options,
   182	    target_release: Option<u64>,
   183	) -> Result<(), String> {
   184	    if !options.flags.contains_key("check") && options.flags.contains_key("verbose") && let Some(n) = previous {
   185	        let old = bound_at(dir.join("releases").join(n.to_string()))?;
   186	        let store = snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::open_read_only(&dir.join("store.sqlite")).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
   187	        let target_label = target_release.map(|n| format!("release {n}")).unwrap_or_else(|| "the new release".into());
   188	        let lines = super::release_narration::compatibility(&store, &old.schema, &bound.schema, n, &target_label, target_release.is_none())?;
   189	        for line in lines {
   190	            eprintln!("{line}");
   191	        }
   192	        if target_release.is_some() {
   193	            for warning in snapback4_lang::client_contracts::compact(&snapback4_lang::client_contracts::compare(&old,bound,&format!("release {n}"))) {
   194	                if snapback4_lang::client_contracts::is_note(&warning) {eprintln!("NOTE {warning}");}
   195	                else {eprintln!("WARNING {warning}");}
   196	            }
   197	        }
   198	    }
   199	    if options.flags.contains_key("allow-destructive") {
   200	        eprintln!(
   201	            "deploy/rollback retain storage; --allow-destructive does not bypass validation or prune. To drop dormant storage: snapback4 prune {} --allow-destructive",
   202	            dir.display()
   203	        );
   204	    }
   205	    Ok(())
   206	}

  788	/// Ask the current retained owner to stop through its private same-owner
  789	/// control socket, then wait until the store lock proves cleanup completed.
  790	pub fn stop_release(options: &Options) -> i32 {
  791	    let result = (|| {
  792	        if crate::store_config::StoreConfig::resolve(options)?.is_some() {
  793	            return Err("E_STORE_UNSUPPORTED: stop is outside the admitted store profile".into());
  794	        }
  795	        let dir = existing_deployment(&directory(options)?)?;
  796	        match crate::release_control::request(&dir, crate::release_control::Command::Stop) {
  797	            Ok(_) => {
  798	                crate::store_owner::wait_released(&dir.join("store.sqlite"), std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))?;
  799	                println!("store stopped: {}", dir.display());
  800	                Ok(())
  801	            }
  802	            Err(control) => match crate::store_owner::wait_released(&dir.join("store.sqlite"), std::time::Duration::ZERO) {
  803	                Ok(()) => {
  804	                    println!("store already stopped: {}", dir.display());
  805	                    Ok(())
  806	                }
  807	                Err(_) => Err(control),
  808	            },
  809	        }
  810	    })();
  811	    match result {
  812	        Ok(()) => 0,
  813	        Err(error) => { eprintln!("stop: {error}"); 1 }
  814	    }
  815	}

   11	pub struct Ceilings {
   12	    pub examined: u64,
   13	    pub index_entries: u64,
   14	    pub rule_probes: u64,

   17	    pub output_bytes: u64,
   18	    pub rows_written: u64,
   19	}
   20	
   21	impl Default for Ceilings {
   22	    fn default() -> Self {
   23	        Self { examined: 8_192, index_entries: 16_384, rule_probes: 8_192, steps: 1_000_000, heap_bytes: 16 << 20, output_bytes: 1 << 20, rows_written: 1_024 }
   24	    }
   25	}
   26	
   27	impl Ceilings {
   28	    /// A job runs one chunk at a time and may write more.
   29	    pub fn job() -> Self {
   30	        Self { rows_written: 8_192, examined: 16_384, ..Self::default() }
   31	    }
   32	
   33	    /// The engine's own partition maintenance is bounded by audience, not by
   34	    /// the author's ceilings.
   35	    pub fn unbounded() -> Self {
   36	        Self { examined: u64::MAX, index_entries: u64::MAX, rule_probes: u64::MAX, steps: u64::MAX, heap_bytes: u64::MAX, output_bytes: u64::MAX, rows_written: u64::MAX }
   37	    }

   39	    fn of(&self, kind: MeterKind) -> u64 {
   40	        match kind {
   41	            MeterKind::Examined => self.examined,
   42	            MeterKind::IndexEntries => self.index_entries,
   43	            MeterKind::RuleProbes => self.rule_probes,
   44	            MeterKind::Steps => self.steps,
   45	            MeterKind::HeapBytes => self.heap_bytes,
   46	            MeterKind::OutputBytes => self.output_bytes,
   47	            MeterKind::RowsWritten => self.rows_written,

   54	pub struct Metered {
   55	    pub examined: u64,
   56	    pub index_entries: u64,
   57	    pub rule_probes: u64,
   58	    pub steps: u64,

   64	impl Metered {
   65	    fn slot(&mut self, kind: MeterKind) -> &mut u64 {
   66	        match kind {
   67	            MeterKind::Examined => &mut self.examined,
   68	            MeterKind::IndexEntries => &mut self.index_entries,
   69	            MeterKind::RuleProbes => &mut self.rule_probes,
   70	            MeterKind::Steps => &mut self.steps,
   71	            MeterKind::HeapBytes => &mut self.heap_bytes,
   72	            MeterKind::OutputBytes => &mut self.output_bytes,
   73	            MeterKind::RowsWritten => &mut self.rows_written,
   74	        }
   75	    }
   76	}

   78	/// How the meter reports a cut: a read site returns what it found so far and
   79	/// marks the result capped; a write aborts.
  137	    }
  138	
  139	    fn resume_read(ceilings: Ceilings, used: Metered, finished: bool) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
  140	        let mut meter = Self::new(ceilings, Cut::Cap);
  141	        meter.at("ordinary search coordinator");
  142	        for (kind, amount) in [(MeterKind::Examined, used.examined), (MeterKind::IndexEntries, used.index_entries),
  143	            (MeterKind::RuleProbes, used.rule_probes), (MeterKind::HeapBytes, used.heap_bytes),
  144	            (MeterKind::OutputBytes, used.output_bytes), (MeterKind::RowsWritten, used.rows_written)] {
  145	            if !meter.charge(kind, amount)? && !(finished && matches!(kind, MeterKind::Examined | MeterKind::IndexEntries | MeterKind::RuleProbes)) {
  146	                return Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind, actual: amount, ceiling: ceilings.of(kind), site: meter.site.clone() });
  147	            }
  148	        }
  149	        meter.step(used.steps)?;
  150	        Ok(meter)
  199	    }

  201	    /// Release a scope whose allocated values have all been dropped, without
  202	    /// erasing work or a refusal. Once-only reservations made in that scope
  203	    /// must be paid again after their heap allowance is released.
  204	    pub(crate) fn release_heap(&mut self, mark: MeterMark) {
  205	        self.used.heap_bytes = mark.used.heap_bytes;
  206	        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
  207	        { self.heap_once = mark.heap_once; }
  208	    }
  209	
  210	    /// Release only the store/row/key scratch part of an incremental scan.
  211	    /// Retained cursor, selected row and buffer allowances are charged
  212	    /// separately; filter allocations and helper bindings remain cumulative.
  213	    pub(crate) fn release_row_heap(&mut self, mark: MeterMark, bytes: u64) {
  214	        self.used.heap_bytes = self.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(bytes);
  215	        #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
  216	        { self.heap_once = mark.heap_once; }
  217	        #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]
  218	        { let _ = mark; }
  219	    }
  220	
  222	    pub fn room(&self, kind: MeterKind, amount: u64) -> bool {
  223	        let used = match kind {
  224	            MeterKind::Examined => self.used.examined,
  225	            MeterKind::IndexEntries => self.used.index_entries,
  226	            MeterKind::RuleProbes => self.used.rule_probes,
  227	            MeterKind::Steps => self.used.steps,
  228	            MeterKind::HeapBytes => self.used.heap_bytes,
  229	            MeterKind::OutputBytes => self.used.output_bytes,
  230	            MeterKind::RowsWritten => self.used.rows_written,
  231	        };
  232	        used.saturating_add(amount) <= self.ceilings.of(kind)
  233	    }

  235	    /// A scalar cannot substitute absence or a partial total for unfinished work.
  236	    pub(crate) fn require_uncapped(&self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
  252	    }
  253	
  254	    pub fn heap(&mut self, bytes: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
  255	        // Heap exhaustion must unwind allocation, even for a capped read.
  256	        // Runner turns that unwind into an incomplete, unavailable result.
  257	        if !self.charge(MeterKind::HeapBytes, bytes)? {
  258	            return Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind: MeterKind::HeapBytes, actual: self.used.heap_bytes, ceiling: self.ceilings.heap_bytes, site: self.site.clone() });
  259	        }
  260	        Ok(())
  261	    }

  323	        for cut in [Cut::Cap, Cut::Abort] {

  334	            meter.once(HeapSite::SqliteColumns, 8192).unwrap();

  337	            assert!(next_read.once(HeapSite::SqliteColumns, 8192).is_err());

    1	use super::Tx;
    2	use crate::{RuntimeError, authority::SessionScope, engine::session_clock::{ClockMint, ClockSession, SessionClockTransaction, PAGE}};
    3	use rusqlite::params;

    5	impl SessionClockTransaction for Tx<'_> {
    6	    fn clock_sessions(&self, read: bool, after: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<ClockSession>, RuntimeError> {
    7	        if read && !super::identity::present(self.conn())? { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
    8	        let sql = if read {
    9	            "SELECT token_digest,created_at FROM _read_sessions WHERE (?1 IS NULL OR token_digest > ?1) ORDER BY token_digest LIMIT ?2"
   10	        } else {
   11	            "SELECT token_digest,created_at FROM _sessions WHERE (?1 IS NULL OR token_digest > ?1) AND COALESCE(family,token_digest) NOT IN (SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key = 'worker:session-family' UNION SELECT substr(key,15) FROM _meta WHERE key LIKE 'worker:family:%') ORDER BY token_digest LIMIT ?2"
   12	        };
   13	        Ok(self.conn().prepare_cached(sql)?.query_map(params![after, PAGE as i64], |r| Ok(ClockSession { digest: r.get(0)?, created_at: r.get(1)? }))?.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?)
   14	    }

FILE snapback4/packages/snapback4/src/session-timing.ts
    1	import type { Session } from "./auth.ts";
    2	import { isReadToken } from "./read-token.ts";
    4	/** Authenticated development and staging return this exact bearer's current live lifetime.
    5	 * Matching the dispatch bearer is the caller's responsibility. Same-bearer
    6	 * preservation is monotonic, so a delayed old reply cannot undo a jump. */
    7	export function reconciledTiming(session: Session, response: Response): Session {
    8	  if (response.headers.get("x-snapback-session-timing") !== "staging") return session;
    9	  const expiry = Number(response.headers.get("x-snapback-session-expires"));
   10	  const capText = response.headers.get("x-snapback-session-cap");
   11	  const cap = capText === null ? undefined : Number(capText);
   12	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(expiry) || expiry <= 0) return session;
   13	  const read = isReadToken(session.token);
   14	  if (read && (cap === undefined || !Number.isSafeInteger(cap) || cap < expiry)) return session;
   15	  if (!read && cap !== undefined) return session;
   16	  const expiresAt = Math.max(session.expiresAt, expiry);
   17	  const capExpiresAt = cap === undefined ? undefined : Math.max(session.capExpiresAt ?? 0, cap);
   18	  if (expiresAt === session.expiresAt && capExpiresAt === session.capExpiresAt) return session;
   19	  return { ...session, expiresAt, ...(capExpiresAt === undefined ? {} : { capExpiresAt }) };
   20	}
   22	export function requestMatchesSession(request: { url: string; authorization: string | null }, base: string, session: Session): boolean {
   23	  return (request.url === base || request.url.startsWith(base + "/")) && request.authorization === `Bearer ${session.token}`;
   24	}
   26	/** Expired local metadata may be superseded by a preserving development or staging jump.
   27	 * Read-only probing creates no session and never widens or refreshes one. */
   28	export async function restoreStagingTiming(base: string, session: Session, fetcher: typeof fetch): Promise<Session | null> {
   29	  const aborter = new AbortController();
   30	  const timer = setTimeout(() => aborter.abort(), 10_000);
   31	  (timer as { unref?: () => void }).unref?.();
   32	  try {
   33	    const response = await fetcher(`${base}/probe?scope=1`, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${session.token}` }, signal: aborter.signal });
   34	    if (!response.ok) return null;
   35	    const next = reconciledTiming(session, response);
   36	    const stamp = Number(response.headers.get("x-snapback-time"));
   37	    if (next === session || !Number.isSafeInteger(stamp) || next.expiresAt <= stamp) return null;
   38	    // Consume the bounded ordinary probe body before blessing restoration.
   39	    const { readResponse } = await import("./http-response.ts");
   40	    const body = await readResponse(response);
   41	    return body.ok === true && body.viewer === session.principal && body.scope === (isReadToken(session.token) ? "read" : "full") ? next : null;
   42	  } catch { return null; }
   43	  finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
   44	}

    12	fn accepts_in(old: &A, new: &A, old_bound: Option<&Bound>, new_bound: Option<&Bound>) -> bool {
    13	    if old==new {return true;}
    14	    match (old,new) {
    15	        (A::Optional(a),A::Optional(b))=>accepts_in(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
    16	        (A::Optional(_),_)=>false,
    17	        (a,A::Optional(b))=>accepts_in(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
    18	        (A::Ref{table:old},A::Ref{table:new})=>new_bound.is_some_and(|bound|bound.schema.table_renames.get(new)==Some(old))
    19	            && old_bound.is_some_and(|bound|bound.schema.table(old).is_some()),
    20	        (A::Text{min:a,max:b,format:af},A::Text{min:c,max:d,format:bf})=>c<=a && d>=b && (bf.is_none() || af==bf),
    21	        (A::IntRange{..},A::Int)=>true,
    22	        (A::IntRange{min:a,max:b},A::IntRange{min:c,max:d})=>c<=a && d>=b,
    23	        (A::Enum{variants:a},A::Enum{variants:b})=>a.iter().all(|v|b.contains(v)),
    24	        (A::Bytes{max:a},A::Bytes{max:b}) | (A::Image{max:a},A::Image{max:b}) |
    25	        (A::Video{max:a},A::Video{max:b})=>b>=a,
    26	        (A::Json{max_bytes:a},A::Json{max_bytes:b})=>b>=a,
    27	        (A::File{max:a,types:at},A::File{max:b,types:bt})=>b>=a && snapback4_core::assets::FILE_TYPES.iter().all(|t|!snapback4_core::assets::file_accepts(at,t)||snapback4_core::assets::file_accepts(bt,t)),
    28	        (A::List{..}|A::ListRange{..},A::List{..}|A::ListRange{..})=> {
    29	            let parts=|t:&A|match t {A::List{of,max}=>(0,*max,of.clone()),A::ListRange{of,min,max}=>(*min,*max,of.clone()),_=>unreachable!()};
    30	            let (a,b,at)=parts(old);let(c,d,bt)=parts(new);
    31	            c<=a && d>=b && match(at,bt){(_,None)=>true,(Some(a),Some(b))=>accepts_in(&a,&b,old_bound,new_bound),_=>false}
    32	        }
    33	        _=>false,
    34	    }
    35	}

    37	#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    38	enum ResultChange { Same, Additive, Changed }
    39	
    40	fn combine(fields: impl IntoIterator<Item=ResultChange>, extra: bool) -> ResultChange {
    41	    let mut additive=extra;
    42	    for field in fields {
    43	        match field {ResultChange::Changed=>return ResultChange::Changed,ResultChange::Additive=>additive=true,ResultChange::Same=>{}}
    44	    }
    45	    if additive {ResultChange::Additive} else {ResultChange::Same}
    46	}

    48	fn table_fields(name: &str, bound: &Bound) -> Option<BTreeMap<String,String>> {
    49	    let schema=bound.schema.public_projection();
    50	    let table=schema.tables.get(name)?;
    51	    Some(table.columns.iter().filter(|(n,_)|!table.engine_field(n)).map(|(n,t)|(n.clone(),format!("{t:?};private={};constraints={:?}",table.read_optional(n),table.constraints.iter().filter(|c|matches!(c,snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Text{field,..} if field==n)).collect::<Vec<_>>()))).collect())
    52	}
    53	
    54	fn map_change<T>(old: &BTreeMap<String,T>, new: &BTreeMap<String,T>, compare: impl Fn(&T,&T)->ResultChange) -> ResultChange {
    55	    combine(old.iter().map(|(name,old)|new.get(name).map(|new|compare(old,new)).unwrap_or(ResultChange::Changed)),new.len()>old.len())
    56	}
    57	
    58	fn result_change(old: &Ty, new: &Ty, old_bound: &Bound, new_bound: &Bound) -> ResultChange {
    59	    if result(old,old_bound)==result(new,new_bound) {return ResultChange::Same;}
    60	    match (old,new) {
    61	        (Ty::Optional(a),Ty::Optional(b))|(Ty::Omittable(a),Ty::Omittable(b))
    62	        |(Ty::List(a,_),Ty::List(b,_))|(Ty::Collection(a,_),Ty::Collection(b,_))=>result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
    63	        (Ty::Object(a)|Ty::RowShape(a)|Ty::RowObject(a),Ty::Object(b)|Ty::RowShape(b)|Ty::RowObject(b))=>map_change(a,b,|a,b|result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound)),
    64	        (Ty::Row(a),Ty::Row(b)) | (Ty::WriteRow(a),Ty::WriteRow(b)) | (Ty::Page(a,_),Ty::Page(b,_)) if a==b=>{
    65	            let (Some(a),Some(b))=(table_fields(a,old_bound),table_fields(b,new_bound)) else{return ResultChange::Changed;};
    66	            combine(a.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if b.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),b.len()>a.len())
    67	        }
    68	        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
    69	    }
    70	}

    72	fn action_result_change(old: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>, new: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>) -> ResultChange {
    73	    match (old,new) {
    74	        (None,None)=>ResultChange::Same,
    75	        (Some(old),Some(new))=>combine(old.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if new.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),new.len()>old.len()),
    76	        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
    77	    }

   101	fn refusals(p: &BoundProgram) -> Vec<String> {
   102	    fn walk(v: &serde_json::Value, out: &mut Vec<String>) {
   103	        match v {
   104	            serde_json::Value::Object(o)=> {
   105	                if let Some(r)=o.get("Require") {out.push(format!("{}:{}",r["code"],r["message"]));}
   106	                for v in o.values(){walk(v,out);}
   107	            }
   108	            serde_json::Value::Array(a)=>for v in a{walk(v,out);},
   109	            _=>{}
   110	        }
   111	    }
   112	    let mut out=Vec::new();walk(&serde_json::to_value(&p.program.body).unwrap(),&mut out);out
   113	}

    12	pub(super) fn kinds(sql: &str, schema: &Schema, count: usize, retained: bool) -> Result<Vec<Kind>, String> {
    13	    let mut tables: Tables = schema.visible_tables().map(|(name, table)| {
    14	        let mut columns = vec![("id".into(), Kind::Plain)];
    15	        columns.extend(table.columns.iter().filter(|(name, _)| *name != "id")

    17	        if retained {columns.extend([("_snapback_state".into(),Kind::Plain),("_snapback_source".into(),Kind::Plain),("_snapback_columns".into(),Kind::Plain)]);}
    18	        (name.to_ascii_lowercase(), columns)
    19	    }).collect();
    20	    let statements = Parser::parse_sql(&SQLiteDialect {}, sql).map_err(|e| format!("--json-objects SQL projection: {e}; use --json for SQLite-specific syntax"))?;

    22	    let columns = query_columns(query, &mut tables)?;
    23	    if columns.len() != count { return Err("--json-objects cannot determine this projection's column types; select explicit columns or use --json".into()); }
    24	    Ok(columns.into_iter().map(|(_, kind)| kind).collect())

    27	fn name(name: &ObjectName) -> Option<String> {
    28	    // SQLite schema qualification bypasses CTE shadowing; do not erase it.
    29	    if name.0.len() != 1 { return None; }
    30	    name.0.last()?.as_ident().map(|id| id.value.to_ascii_lowercase())
    31	}
