    33	fn query_columns(query: &Query, inherited: &mut Tables) -> Result<Columns, String> {
    34	    let mut tables = inherited.clone();
    35	    if let Some(with) = &query.with {
    36	        if with.recursive { return Err("--json-objects does not infer recursive CTE types; use --json".into()); }
    37	        for cte in &with.cte_tables {
    38	            if tables.contains_key(&cte.alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()) {
    39	                return Err("--json-objects does not infer shadowing CTEs; use --json".into());
    40	            }
    41	            let mut columns = query_columns(&cte.query, &mut tables)?;
    42	            for (column, alias) in columns.iter_mut().zip(&cte.alias.columns) { column.0 = alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase(); }
    43	            tables.insert(cte.alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase(), columns);
    44	        }
    45	    }
    46	    set_columns(&query.body, &mut tables)
    47	}
    48	
    49	fn relation(factor: &TableFactor, tables: &mut Tables) -> Result<(String, Columns), String> {
    50	    match factor {
    51	        TableFactor::Table { name: object, alias, args: None, .. } => {
    52	            let key = name(object).ok_or("--json-objects does not infer schema-qualified relations; use --json")?;
    53	            let columns = tables.get(&key).ok_or("--json-objects needs application tables or typed CTEs")?.clone();
    54	            Ok((alias.as_ref().map(|a| a.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()).unwrap_or(key), columns))
    55	        }
    56	        TableFactor::Derived { subquery, alias, .. } => Ok((alias.as_ref().map(|a| a.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()).unwrap_or_default(), query_columns(subquery, tables)?)),
    57	        _ => Err("--json-objects cannot infer this table expression; use --json".into()),
    58	    }
    59	}
    60	
    61	fn set_columns(body: &SetExpr, tables: &mut Tables) -> Result<Columns, String> {
    62	    match body {
    63	        SetExpr::Query(q) => query_columns(q, tables),
    64	        SetExpr::SetOperation { left, right, .. } => {
    65	            let mut left = set_columns(left, tables)?;
    66	            let right = set_columns(right, tables)?;
    67	            if left.len() != right.len() { return Err("incompatible SQL projections".into()); }
    68	            for (l, r) in left.iter_mut().zip(right) { if l.1 != r.1 { l.1 = Kind::Plain; } }
    69	            Ok(left)
    70	        }
    71	        SetExpr::Select(select) => {
    72	            let mut sources = Vec::new();
    73	            for from in &select.from {
    74	                sources.push(relation(&from.relation, tables)?);
    75	                for join in &from.joins { sources.push(relation(&join.relation, tables)?); }
    76	            }
    77	            let mut output = Vec::new();
    78	            for item in &select.projection {
    79	                match item {
    80	                    SelectItem::Wildcard(_) => output.extend(sources.iter().flat_map(|(_, cols)| cols.clone())),
    81	                    SelectItem::QualifiedWildcard(SelectItemQualifiedWildcardKind::ObjectName(object), _) => {
    82	                        let key = name(object).ok_or("unsupported wildcard")?;
    83	                        let (_, cols) = sources.iter().find(|(alias, _)| *alias == key).ok_or("unknown wildcard table")?;
    84	                        output.extend(cols.clone());
    85	                    }
    86	                    SelectItem::UnnamedExpr(expr) => {
    87	                        let mut direct = expr;
    88	                        while let Expr::Nested(inner) = direct { direct = inner; }
    89	                        let label = match direct {
    90	                            Expr::Identifier(id) => id.value.clone(),
    91	                            Expr::CompoundIdentifier(ids) => ids.last().unwrap().value.clone(),
    92	                            _ => expr.to_string(),
    93	                        };
    94	                        output.push((label.to_ascii_lowercase(), kind(expr, &sources)));
    95	                    }
    96	                    SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr, alias } => output.push((alias.value.to_ascii_lowercase(), kind(expr, &sources))),
    97	                    _ => return Err("unsupported object-row projection; use --json".into()),
    98	                }
    99	            }
   100	            let mut names = BTreeSet::new();
   101	            if output.iter().any(|(name, _)| !names.insert(name)) {
   102	                return Err("--json-objects needs unique names in every projection; alias duplicate columns".into());
   103	            }
   104	            Ok(output)
   105	        }
   106	        _ => Err("--json-objects needs a SELECT projection; use --json".into()),
   107	    }
   108	}
   109	
   110	fn kind(expr: &Expr, sources: &[(String, Columns)]) -> Kind {
   111	    let (table, column) = match expr {
   112	        Expr::Nested(expr) => return kind(expr, sources),
   113	        Expr::Identifier(id) => (None, &id.value),
   114	        Expr::CompoundIdentifier(ids) if ids.len() == 2 => (Some(ids[0].value.to_ascii_lowercase()), &ids[1].value),
   115	        _ => return Kind::Plain, // Computed SQL expressions retain SQLite's own types.
   116	    };
   117	    let found: Vec<Kind> = sources.iter().filter(|(alias, _)| table.as_ref().is_none_or(|t| t == alias))
   118	        .flat_map(|(_, cols)| cols.iter().filter(|(name, _)| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(column)).map(|(_, kind)| *kind)).collect();
   119	    // An unqualified duplicate only reaches execution when SQLite resolved it
   120	    // through USING/NATURAL. All contributors must agree before typing it bool.
   121	    found.first().copied().filter(|first| found.iter().all(|kind| kind == first)).unwrap_or(Kind::Plain)
   122	}

     7	export function changelogFlags(changelog) {
     8	  // Changelog entries are newest first. The newest mention decides whether
     9	  // an option is supported; explicit retirement prose must not announce it.
    10	  const flags = new Map();
    11	  for (const line of changelog.split('\n')) {
    12	    let verb, packageManagerCommand = false;
    13	    const retired = [...line.matchAll(/\b(?:drops?|dropped|removes?|removed|retires?|retired)\s+(?:(?:the|unsupported)\s+)*[A-Za-z-]+\s+--[a-z][a-z-]*/gi)];
    14	    // Every flag must follow a named owner; preserve owner through adjacent flags.
    15	    // Exact's rebuild command is an external tool, explicitly outside binary help.
    16	    for (const match of line.matchAll(/\b(?:exact\.mjs|[A-Za-z]+)\b|--[a-z][a-z0-9-]*/g)) {
    17	      const token = match[0];
    18	      if (['npm', 'bun', 'pnpm'].includes(token)) {
    19	        verb = 'package-manager';
    20	        packageManagerCommand = true;
    21	      }
    22	      else if (token === 'exact.mjs') verb = 'exact';
    23	      else if (verbs.has(token.toLowerCase())) {
    24	        // `run` immediately after npm/bun/pnpm names the package-manager
    25	        // subcommand. A later explicit Snapback verb still starts a new owner.
    26	        if (packageManagerCommand && token.toLowerCase() === 'run') packageManagerCommand = false;
    27	        else {
    28	          verb = token.toLowerCase();
    29	          packageManagerCommand = false;
    30	        }
    31	      }
    32	      else if (token.startsWith('--')) {
    33	        if (verb === 'package-manager' || verb === 'exact' && token === '--rebuild') continue;
    34	        if (!verb || verb === 'exact') throw new Error(`changelog flag ${token} needs an explicit Snapback verb: ${line}`);
    35	        const key = `${verb} ${token}`;
    36	        if (!flags.has(key)) flags.set(key, retired.some(span => match.index >= span.index && match.index < span.index + span[0].length) ? null : [verb, token]);
    37	      }
    38	      else packageManagerCommand = false;
    39	    }
    40	  }
    41	  return [...flags.values()].filter(Boolean);
    42	}
    43	export function assertChangelogHelp(changelog, help) {
    44	  const failures = [];
    45	  for (const [verb, flag] of changelogFlags(changelog)) {
    46	    const output = help(verb);
    47	    if (!new RegExp(`${flag}(?![a-z0-9-])`).test(output)) failures.push(`${verb} --help omits announced ${flag}`);
    48	  }
    49	  if (failures.length) throw new Error(failures.join('\n'));
    50	}

    52	  const cache = new Map();

    56	      if (result.status !== 0) throw new Error(`${verb} --help failed: ${result.stderr}`);
    57	      cache.set(verb, result.stdout);

     2	use crate::{error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError}, meter::Meter, schema::{ColumnDefault, IndexComponent, Maintain, Table}, value::{Value, InternalPrice}};

     6	/// Cumulative callback work per source row. Admission adds one examination;
     7	/// heap is checked separately because row scratch is released after each row.
     8	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
     9	pub(crate) struct Work {
    10	    pub examined: u64,
    11	    pub steps: u64,
    12	    pub index_entries: u64,
    13	}
    14	
    15	impl Work {
    16	    pub const DECODE: Self = Self { examined: 1, steps: 0, index_entries: 0 };
    17	
    18	    pub fn with_contribution(mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Self {
    19	        self.examined = self.examined.saturating_add(1);
    20	        self.steps = self.steps.saturating_add(maintain.evaluation_steps());
    21	        // A selected contribution creates exactly one entry, otherwise none.
    22	        self.index_entries = self.index_entries.saturating_add(1);
    23	        self
    24	    }
    25	
    26	    pub fn table(table: &Table) -> Self {
    27	        table.indexes.values().fold(Self::DECODE, |work, index| match index.components.first() {
    28	            Some(IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) => work.with_contribution(maintain),
    29	            _ => work,
    30	        })
    31	    }
    32	
    33	    fn counters(self, meter: &Meter) -> [(MeterKind, u64, u64, u64); 3] {
    34	        [
    35	            (MeterKind::Examined, self.examined.saturating_add(1), meter.used.examined, meter.ceilings.examined),
    36	            (MeterKind::Steps, self.steps, meter.used.steps, meter.ceilings.steps),
    37	            (MeterKind::IndexEntries, self.index_entries, meter.used.index_entries, meter.ceilings.index_entries),
    38	        ]
    39	    }
    40	
    41	    pub fn limit(self, meter: &Meter, maximum: usize) -> usize {
    42	        self.counters(meter).into_iter().filter(|(_, per_row, _, _)| *per_row != 0)
    43	            .fold(maximum as u64, |limit, (_, per_row, used, ceiling)| limit.min(ceiling.saturating_sub(used) / per_row))
    44	            // An empty range is still legal; a non-fitting singleton refuses
    45	            // in fits(), after establishing that there really is a source row.
    46	            .max(1) as usize
    47	    }
    48	
    49	    fn fits(self, meter: &Meter, count: usize) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    50	        for (kind, per_row, used, ceiling) in self.counters(meter) {
    51	            let actual = used.saturating_add(per_row.saturating_mul(count as u64));
    52	            if actual > ceiling {
    53	                if count > 1 { return Ok(false); }
    54	                return Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind, actual, ceiling, site: meter.site().to_owned() });
    55	            }
    56	        }
    57	        Ok(true)
    58	    }
    59	}

    61	pub(crate) fn decode_bytes(data: &str) -> InternalPrice {
    62	    InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut Meter::new(crate::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort), |_, scope| heap::stored_row(data, scope).fixed(4096))
    63	}

    65	/// The price remains opaque: adoption may charge it only on its internal meter.
    66	pub(crate) fn contribution_bytes(row: &Value, table: &Table) -> InternalPrice {
    67	    InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut Meter::new(crate::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort), |_, scope| {
    68	        let mut bytes = row.retained_internal(scope);
    69	        for (name, kind) in &table.columns {
    70	            if row.field(name).is_ok() { continue; }
    71	            let added = if table.maintained.contains_key(name) || kind.is_optional() { Some(InternalPrice::zero()) }
    72	                else if let Some(ColumnDefault::Literal(value)) = table.defaults.get(name) { Some(value.retained_internal(scope)) }
    73	                else { None };
    74	            if let Some(added) = added { bytes = bytes.fixed(80 + name.len() as u64).plus(added); }
    75	        }
    76	        bytes.times(4).fixed(4096)
    77	    })
    78	}

    82	}
    83	pub(crate) fn fits(meter: &mut Meter, price: &InternalPrice) -> bool {
    84	    InternalLedger::with_meter(meter, |meter, scope| price.fits(meter, scope))

    87	// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9.3 — shrink pages before adoption writes when retained images plus row work cannot fit.
    88	#[cfg(feature="postgres")]
    89	pub(crate) fn page_fits<'a>(images: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a str>, meter: &mut Meter,
    90	    work: Work, scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value) -> InternalPrice>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    91	    let checked=|row:&Value|Ok(scratch.map_or_else(InternalPrice::zero,|f|f(row)));
    92	    page_fits_checked(images,meter,work,scratch.map(|_|&checked as &dyn Fn(&Value)->Result<InternalPrice,RuntimeError>))
    93	}
    94	
    95	pub(crate) fn page_fits_checked<'a>(images: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a str>, meter: &mut Meter,
    96	    work: Work, scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value) -> Result<InternalPrice,RuntimeError>>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    97	    // Fix every cumulative budget before admission decodes or callbacks. Heap
    98	    // retries retain used work, so both this check and limit use the remainder.
    99	    if !work.fits(meter, images.len())? { return Ok(false); }
   100	    let singleton = images.len() == 1;
   101	    for data in images {
   102	        let mark = meter.mark();
   103	        let decode = decode_bytes(data);
   104	        if !singleton && !fits(meter, &decode) { return Ok(false); }
   105	        charge(meter, decode)?;
   106	        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   107	        let row: Option<Value> = scratch.map(|_| crate::json_codec::from_text(data).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))).transpose()?;
   108	        let work = match (scratch, row.as_ref()) { (Some(scratch), Some(row)) => scratch(row)?, _ => InternalPrice::zero() };
   109	        let fits = fits(meter, &work);
   110	        // Only a singleton may refuse for heap. Larger pages can be dropped
   111	        // and fetched again with a smaller limit, without replaying a write.
   112	        if !fits && singleton { charge(meter, work)?; }
   113	        drop(row);
   114	        meter.release_heap(mark);
   115	        if !fits { return Ok(false); }
   116	    }
   117	    Ok(true)
   118	}

   120	/// Full simultaneous old/new key-vector scratch, including bounded token
   121	/// cardinality. Live destinations are plain; captured/manual successors may
   122	/// add word indexes and must still be admitted before native index_write.
   123	pub(crate) fn index_capacity(table:&Table)->u64 {
   124	    table.indexes.values().map(|i|index_copies(table,i)).fold(0_u64,u64::saturating_add)
   125	}
   126	fn index_copies(table:&Table,index:&crate::schema::Index)->u64 {
   127	    if let Some((_,fields))=index.word_component() {
   128	        fields.iter().filter_map(|f|table.columns.get(f)).map(|k|match k.required(){crate::schema::ColumnType::Text{max}=>u64::from(*max),crate::schema::ColumnType::Enum{variants}=>variants.iter().map(|s|s.len() as u64).max().unwrap_or(0),_=>0}).fold(0_u64,u64::saturating_add).min(crate::words::MAX_TOKENS_PER_ROW as u64)
   129	    }else{1}
   130	}
   131	pub(crate) fn index_scratch(name:&str,table:&Table)->u64 {
   132	    table.indexes.iter().map(|(label,index)| {
   133	        // Legacy oversized keys may legally remain equal or shrink. Their
   134	        // buffers still coexist; the ordinary 2048-byte gate is not a bound
   135	        // on allocation before that gate runs.
   136	        let key=index.components.iter().fold(291_u64,|n,c|n.saturating_add(match c {
   137	            IndexComponent::Column(field)=>table.columns.get(field).and_then(crate::schema::live::key_column).unwrap_or_else(||super::disclosed::decode_reservation(table)),
   138	            IndexComponent::WordPrefixes{..}=>2*crate::words::MAX_TOKEN_BYTES as u64+3,
   139	            _=>super::disclosed::decode_reservation(table),
   140	        })).max(super::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as u64);
   141	        // Empty token sets still allocate an IndexWrite slot and the word
   142	        // field-reference vector. These are independent of emitted key count.
   143	        let fixed=512_u64.saturating_add(4*(name.len()+label.len()) as u64)
   144	            .saturating_add(index.word_component().map_or(0,|(_,fields)|(fields.len() as u64).saturating_mul(32)));
   145	        fixed.saturating_add(index_copies(table,index).saturating_mul(key.saturating_mul(4).saturating_add(128*(index.components.len() as u64+1)+512+4*(name.len()+label.len()) as u64)))
   146	    }).fold(0_u64,u64::saturating_add)
   147	}

    46	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — reconcile the exact bearer before the SDK observes advanced business time.
    47	pub(super) fn session_clock_headers(request: &Request, shared: &Shared) -> Vec<Header> {
    48	    if !shared.staging && !shared.personas { return clock_headers(shared).into(); }
    49	    let Ok(token) = crate::auth::bearer_token(request) else { return clock_headers(shared).into(); };
    50	    // Detached readers never fall back to the writer: callers may still hold it.
    51	    // Keep the process clock fixed across the committed authority snapshot, so
    52	    // preserved lifetime and the clock stamp describe the same staging jump.
    53	    let Ok((epoch, reader)) = shared.reader() else {
    54	        return vec![Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Timing", "unavailable").unwrap()];
    55	    };
    56	    let identity = lock(&shared.wake).store_id.clone();
    57	    let clock = lock(&shared.clock);
    58	    let now = clock.now().max(shared.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire));
    59	    let timing = identity.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Auth("store identity unavailable".into()))
    60	        .and_then(|identity| reader.staging_session_timing(token, now, identity));
    61	    let headers = match timing {
    62	        Ok(timing) => {
    63	            let mut headers = vec![Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Timing", "staging").unwrap(),
    64	                Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Time", now.to_string()).unwrap(),
    65	                Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Clock", clock.revision()).unwrap()];
    66	            if let Some(timing) = timing {
    67	                headers.push(Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Expires", timing.expires_at.to_string()).unwrap());
    68	                if let Some(cap) = timing.cap_expires_at { headers.push(Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Cap", cap.to_string()).unwrap()); }
    69	            }
    70	            headers
    71	        }
    72	        Err(_) => vec![Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Timing", "unavailable").unwrap()],
    73	    };
    74	    drop(clock);
    75	    lock(&shared.readers).put(&epoch, reader.into_inner());
    76	    headers
    77	}
    78	
    79	pub(crate) fn clock_headers(shared: &Shared) -> [Header; 2] {
    80	    let clock = lock(&shared.clock);
    81	    let now = clock.now().max(shared.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire));
    82	    [Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Time", now.to_string()).unwrap(),
    83	     Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Clock", clock.revision()).unwrap()]
    84	}

    11	pub(crate) fn typescript(project:&Project,bound:&Bound)->io::Result<String>{
    12	    let(text,warnings)=report(project,bound)?;
    13	    for warning in warnings {
    14	        if snapback4_lang::client_contracts::is_note(&warning) {eprintln!("NOTE {warning}");}

    16	    }

    19	pub(crate) fn report(project: &Project, bound: &Bound) -> io::Result<(String,Vec<String>)> {
    20	    let path = project.root.join("snapback/client-compatibility.json");
    21	    let text = match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
    22	        Ok(text) => text,
    23	        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok((snapback4_lang::emit::typescript(bound),Vec::new())),
    24	        Err(error) => return Err(error),
    25	    };
    26	    let bad = |message: String| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, format!("client-compatibility.json: {message}; guide deploy"));
    27	    let config: Configuration = serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|e| bad(e.to_string()))?;
    28	    if config.since_release == 0 { return Err(bad("since_release must be a positive release label".into())); }
    29	    let path = project.root.join(&config.baseline);
    30	    let absolute = std::path::absolute(&path)?;
    31	    let origin = format!("resolved from {} at project root {}", project.root.join("snapback/client-compatibility.json").display(), project.root.display());
    32	    let baseline_error = |message| bad(format!("baseline {}: {message} ({origin})", absolute.display()));
    33	    if !path.exists() {
    34	        return Err(bad(format!("baseline {} not saved yet: does not exist ({origin})", absolute.display())));
    35	    }
    36	    let sources = sources(&path).map_err(|e| baseline_error(e.to_string()))?;
    37	    let baseline = snapback4_lang::compile(&sources);
    38	    if !baseline.diagnostics.is_empty() { return Err(baseline_error(format!("saved baseline does not compile: {:?}", baseline.diagnostics))); }
    39	    let warnings=snapback4_lang::client_contracts::compare(&baseline,bound,&format!("baseline {}",absolute.display()));
    40	    Ok((snapback4_lang::emit::typescript_spanning(bound, &baseline, config.since_release),warnings))
    41	}

    43	/// Shared schema-first ordering retains saved modules' original namespaces.
    44	pub(crate) fn sources(path: &std::path::Path) -> io::Result<Vec<(String, String)>> {
    45	    if !path.try_exists()? {return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound,format!("{}: not saved yet: saved source does not exist",path.display())));}
    46	    let bad = |message: &str| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, message);
    47	    let mut paths = if path.is_dir() {
    48	        std::fs::read_dir(path)?.map(|entry| entry.map(|entry| entry.path())).collect::<io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?
    49	            .into_iter().filter(|path| path.is_file() && path.extension().is_some_and(|extension| extension == "q")).collect::<Vec<_>>()
    50	    } else { vec![path.to_owned()] };
    51	    paths.sort_by_key(|path| (path.file_name().is_none_or(|name| name != "schema.q"), path.clone()));

NOT READY

1. **Fan-out forward/reverse processing splits one live allocation across independent job allowances.** [extraction_each.rs:379](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b25-dx8/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/extraction_each.rs:379) walks parents with `activation::walk`, then creates a fresh meter while the fetched parent page remains resident. Child `load` also uses an independent meter. Forward processing follows the same pattern.

   Concrete counterexample: 256 parents with 4 KiB unrelated text retain roughly 3 MiB of serialized page reservations. One parent has 60 native children, each containing an additional 64 KiB text field. Reverse processing reserves at least 15 MiB for those accumulated child images. Both meters individually admit their work, although their simultaneously live reservations exceed the 16 MiB job ceiling.

   **Required correction:** share the walker's meter with fan-out traversal, child decoding and retained scratch; precharge allocations before loading them. Forward and reverse need the same accounting discipline already used by resume.

2. **Frontend cleanup can report success while a serving descendant survives.** [proof.ts:190](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b25-dx8/snapback4/packages/snapback4/src/proof.ts:190) starts frontends with `detached:true` and a liveness pipe, but [proof-process.ts:136](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b25-dx8/snapback4/packages/snapback4/src/proof-process.ts:136) registers groups only for `processGroup:true`. Consequently, `groupGone` immediately succeeds for these frontend handles.

   Concrete counterexample: a Vite plugin starts a serving subprocess in the inherited group. Its keeper exits unexpectedly; `proof-host` then exits, but the subprocess remains. Calling `stop()` observes the exited host and resolves successfully without checking the surviving group. The descendant never left custody.

   **Required correction:** register frontend keeper-backed groups and await bounded group-cleanup evidence on stop and startup failure. Unexpected keeper loss with surviving members must produce an explicit cleanup failure.
